articleOfWeek.title: Positive pressure ventilation in newborns at birth: a systematic review of recipient characteristics and temporal trends.
articleOfWeek.abstract: To synthesise evidence on temporal trends, recipient characteristics and variation in the use of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) at birth. This systematic review was registered (CRD42024487025) and followed a condition-context-population framework. Five electronic databases and grey literature were searched to 25 June 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI checklist, and reporting followed PRISMA 2020. Forty-two studies from 34 countries (27 from high-income countries), reporting 269 to 10,696,831 livebirths per study (1984-2024), were included. Heterogeneity in whether continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was distinguished from PPV, interface definitions and eligibility criteria precluded meta-analysis. Fifteen studies included only preterm infants and 19 excluded congenital anomalies. Nine population-based and large multicentre studies that excluded CPAP and included all age groups reported PPV incidence ranging from 3.0% to 8.0%. Rates were much higher among very and extremely preterm infants. Temporal trends suggested increasing PPV incidence overall and via facemask, whereas tracheal-tube PPV was stable or declining. Lower PPV incidence was reported in low-resource and lower-level birthing centres. Few studies reported indications for or timing of PPV initiation, and reported data items were inconsistent. PPV remains common in neonatal resuscitation, with higher use at lower gestational ages and higher-level birthing services. Limited and heterogeneous reporting of indications and PPV timelines constrains interpretation and comparison. Standardised, neonatal Utstein-aligned reporting, including PPV indications and time intervals and separate reporting of airway interfaces and CPAP, is needed. Further population-based studies, particularly in low-and middle-income countries, are warranted.

articles.title: The Impact of Early Changes in Albumin Levels on Long-Term Kidney and Mortality Outcomes in Patients With Acute Kidney Injury Undergoing Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy.
authors: LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium (LINKA) investigators
articles.abstract: To investigate the association between early changes in the levels of serum albumin during continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) and long-term dialysis dependence and mortality in patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 days or more days after CKRT initiation. A multicenter retrospective cohort study. Eight university-affiliated tertiary hospitals in South Korea participating in the LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium cohort. The study involved 1087 adult patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 or more days after CKRT initiation between January 2017 and June 2022. None. Based on albumin levels at CKRT initiation and on day 7, patients were categorized into the persistent, resolved, new-onset, and no hypoalbuminemia groups. A composite of progression to end-stage kidney disease and all-cause mortality within 365 days was the primary outcome. The composite outcome occurred in 33.4% (363/1087) of the patients. The adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for the primary outcome was significantly higher in all groups when compared with the no hypoalbuminemia group (persistent: aOR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.73-4.04; p < 0.001; resolved: aOR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.38-3.75; p < 0.001; new-onset: aOR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.06-2.68; p = 0.028). No hypoalbuminemia group was associated with the most favorable prognosis, whereas persistent hypoalbuminemia was associated with the worst outcomes. During CKRT, early albumin level changes are associated with long-term kidney failure and mortality risk. Persistent hypoalbuminemia predicts the worst outcomes. Even in patients without baseline hypoalbuminemia, early decline in albumin is associated with worse prognosis.

articles.title: Dynamics of Mitochondrial Structure, Biogenesis and Function in Skeletal Muscle of Critically Ill Patients.
articles.abstract: To define the timing and phenotype of mitochondrial ultrastructural remodeling and electron transport chain (ETC) function in skeletal muscle during early critical illness. Secondary analysis of a prospective observational study with serial muscle biopsies. Adult ICU. Thirty-three mechanically ventilated ICU patients (median age, 49 yr; 27% women) with Sequential Organ Failure Assessment greater than or equal to 9 on three consecutive days; skeletal muscle biopsies of the vastus lateralis muscle at ICU day 5 (n = 29) and day 15 (n = 22). Healthy subjects served as controls. None. Vastus lateralis biopsies were analyzed by electron microscopy with stereology, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blotting, and spectrophotometric ETC enzyme assays (reported per tissue weight and normalized to citrate synthase [CS]). Intact mitochondrial profiles were reduced vs. controls (fold change vs. controls: day 5, 0.24 [0.18-0.34]; p = 0.039 and day 15, 0.20 [0.16-0.33]; p = 0.011) and disturbed profiles increased (day 5, 5.62 [3.20-7.17]; p < 0.001 and day 15, 5.20 [3.67-6.36]; p = 0.001), with reduced volume density of intact mitochondria (day 5, 0.33 [0.20-0.49]; p = 0.009 and day 15, 0.32 [0.21-0.50]; p = 0.005). Inner mitochondrial membrane surface-to-volume ratio was reduced at day 5 (0.69 [0.49-0.89]; p = 0.022) and remained unchanged at day 15. Complex III tissue activity was reduced at day 5 (85.6 [22.1-133.3] vs. 151.4 [100.5-205.0]; p = 0.015) and day 15 (50.5 [36.0-69.8]; p = 0.001), remaining reduced after CS normalization (day 5, 0.83 [0.34-1.49]; p = 0.040 and day 15, 0.87 [0.65-0.93]; p = 0.007). Complex IV activity remained reduced before and after CS normalization at both time points (all p < 0.001). CS activity declined by day 15 (56.3 [52.7-65.1] vs. 95.6 [80.1-133.0]; p = 0.001 and day 15 vs. day 5; p = 0.041). qRT-PCR and Western blot supported reduced ETC components and altered biogenesis signaling. Skeletal muscle mitochondrial ultrastructure is altered by ICU day 5 and remains abnormal at day 15, with persistent complex III/IV dysfunction after CS normalization. These findings define an early sustained mitochondrial remodeling phenotype in skeletal muscle during critical illness.

articles.title: Language Concordance in Critical Care: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Language barriers are associated with differences in care delivery processes and outcomes in critical care settings, with differences despite language assistance services. Less is known about outcomes associated with language concordant care. Language concordance is a linguistic match between a patient's preferred language and the language used by their care team. We undertook a systematic review to examine the measurement and impact of language concordant care delivery during critical illness, inclusive of the critical care recovery period after hospitalization. A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Embase, and Cochrane of English-language publications from database inception to March 3, 2026. Studies that investigated adults in critical care and post-ICU recovery clinic settings that included measurement of language concordance were included. Study quality was evaluated by the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. Of 1,682 unique records identified, 11 were eligible for inclusion (128,181 total patients; mean [sd] age, 68.4 [17.9 yr]; 72,872 [56.9%] male and 55,082 [43.1%] female). Six studies assessed clinical decision-making. Reported outcomes included code status changes, family conferences, communication complexity, delirium, length of stay, mechanical ventilation, and mortality. Due to significant heterogeneity in study analyses and reported outcomes, data were not pooled for quantitative analysis. Current evidence suggests that language-concordant care may influence clinically meaningful processes of critical care, warranting interventional studies to guide care delivery recommendations.

articles.title: From pneumonia to ARDS: a dynamic pulmonary-systemic framework.
Prognostic relevance of protein prescriptions based on adjusted body weight in critically ill overweight or obese patients - analysis of a large international database.
articles.abstract: ESPEN currently recommends using adjusted body weight (aBW) to guide protein prescriptions for critically ill overweight or obese patients. The prognostic relevance of this concept is unknown. We analyzed a subset of a large international point prevalence survey of nutritional practice in 785 intensive care units (ICUs) worldwide. Patients were included if they had been in the ICU for at least 96 h and had a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m². We modelled the association between early average protein intake (days 1-4 after ICU admission) and the cause-specific adjusted hazards of in-ICU death and ICU discharge alive within a competing risks framework. Intake was normalized to aBW, defined as ideal body weight plus 25% of the difference between actual and ideal body weight. 9,068 patients were analyzed. There was no evidence of an association between early protein intake and ICU discharge alive. In contrast, very low protein intake (below approximately 0.45 g/kg aBW/day) was associated with a higher hazard of in-ICU death. Above this threshold, there was no clear evidence of a further association between protein intake and the hazard of in-ICU death. The strongest association was observed at 0 g/kg aBW/day (adjusted hazard rate 1.41 i.e. an estimated 38% higher risk, 95% confidence interval 1.17-1.69). Early protein intake does not appear to be associated with time to ICU discharge among survivors. However, in critically ill patients with overweight or obesity, very low protein intake during the early acute phase may be associated with less favorable in-ICU outcomes.

Coronary Perfusion Pressure During Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation is Associated with Outcomes from Pediatric In-hospital Cardiac Arrest.
authors: ICU-Resuscitation Project (ICU-RESUS) Investigators and the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Collaborative Pediatric Critical Care Research Network Investigators
articles.abstract: Multiple animal studies and one adult study establish that coronary perfusion pressure (CoPP) during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is associated with survival outcomes, such as return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Yet, CoPP during pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (pIHCA) has not been investigated. We hypothesized that an average CoPP ≥20mmHg during the first 10 minutes of CPR for pIHCA would be associated with higher rates of ROSC. We performed a secondary analysis of the ICU-RESUScitation trial, a cluster randomized, step-wedged trial of a physiology-focused quality improvement bundle in pIHCA. Index CPR events among patients ≥37 weeks corrected gestational age and <18 years with invasive arterial blood pressure (BP) and central venous pressure (CVP) monitoring were eligible for inclusion. The primary exposure was event-level average CoPP (≥20mmHg vs <20mmHg) during the first 10 minutes of CPR; secondary exposure was CoPP <10 mmHg. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC ≥20 minutes. Multivariable modified Poisson regression with adjustment for confounders evaluated the relationship between CoPP and outcomes. Among 111 included patients, median age was 0.2 years [0.0, 0.6]. Seventy-one (64%) achieved ROSC. Thirty (27%) had CoPP ≥20mmHg. Patients with CoPP ≥20mmHg were more frequently ≥1 year of age and less frequently had congenital heart disease. In adjusted models, average CoPP ≥20mmHg was associated with higher rates of ROSC (aRR 1.48 [95%CI 1.12, 1.95]; p=0.005). CoPP <10 mmHg was associated with lower rates of ROSC. In this first investigation of CoPP during CPR for pIHCA, CoPP ≥20mmHg was associated with ROSC.

articles.title: Cycle-to-Cycle Prediction of Return of Spontaneous Circulation Using End-Tidal Carbon Dioxide Dynamics in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract: Prognostication in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) commonly relies on static pre-resuscitation variables, although resuscitation is a rapidly evolving physiologic process. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) is continuously available during cardiopulmonary resuscitation, but its sequential information has not been fully used for real-time prediction. We aim to develop and internally validate a cycle-to-cycle time-updated prediction model using sequential EtCO2 values to estimate the probability of return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in the subsequent 2-minute resuscitation cycle. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of adult OHCA patients from the NTUH-HYCARD database between 2016 and 2023. Event-level EtCO2 sequences were extracted from resuscitation records and standardized into 2-minute intervals for up to 30 minutes, consistent with Advanced Cardiac Life Support reassessment cycles. At each prediction time point, the model used EtCO2 values available from event onset to the current time point, without using future values. A two-layer long short-term memory model estimated the probability of ROSC in the subsequent cycle. Performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation at two levels: the event level (one prediction per event) and the cycle level (one prediction per 2-minute cycle). The final analysis included 1,651 event-level EtCO2 sequences from 1,480 patients; 583 events ended with ROSC. At the event level, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.876 (95% CI, 0.863-0.890) and a Brier score of 0.140 (95% CI, 0.131-0.149). When applied to every 2-minute cycle (17,029 prediction points; ROSC prevalence, 3.4%), the AUROC was 0.685 (95% CI, 0.664-0.706), and the model systematically overestimated ROSC probability (Brier score, 0.285; 95% CI, 0.268-0.303). Sequential EtCO2 dynamics showed good event-level discrimination for predicting ROSC in the subsequent cycle. When applied at each cycle, the model retained modest discrimination but overestimated ROSC probability, indicating that recalibration is required before cycle-to-cycle use.

articles.title: Resuscitation using fresh-frozen plasma is associated with improved contextual fear memory in a non-TBI mouse model of trauma and hemorrhagic shock.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Cognitive dysfunction is a consequence of traumatic injury with lasting impacts. Even without direct brain injury, trauma and hemorrhagic shock (T/HS) can cause malperfusion, inflammation, and neuronal injury. Disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx (eGC), a key regulator of vascular homeostasis, contributes to trauma-induced endotheliopathy and may influence secondary neurologic injury. Prior work demonstrated that fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) resuscitation preserves eGC expression and reduces maladaptive vascular repair in a murine T/HS model. This study evaluates post-injury cognition and FFP protection against cognitive impairment compared with lactated Ringer's (LR). Male C57BL/6 mice were randomized to sham procedure or T/HS followed by a volume-driven LR or pressure-directed FFP resuscitation approach. T/HS mice underwent laparotomy, femoral artery cannulation, hemorrhagic shock, pseudofractures via bone homogenate injection, and hindlimb muscle crush injuries. Sham mice received laparotomy and femoral artery cutdown. Four days postsurgery, open field testing assessed locomotion, followed by fear conditioning on days 7 to 8 to assess cognition. Brains were collected to analyze hippocampal glycosaminoglycans hyaluronan, heparan sulfate (HS), and chondroitin sulfate (CS). Open field testing showed intact locomotion at post-injury day 4 in all groups. On day 8, mice resuscitated with FFP had significantly greater contextual freezing compared with mice resuscitated with LR, consistent with improved hippocampal-dependent contextual memory. Cued fear conditioning did not differ between groups. LR and FFP resuscitation strategies resulted in distinct hippocampal hyaluronan and HS staining patterns, without synthesis gene expression differences. T/HS+LR brains showed increased 4-O-sulfated CS (CS-4S), a neurologically detrimental sulfation pattern, whereas FFP decreased CS-4S and increased CS-6S. Goal-directed plasma resuscitation is associated with improved spatial memory and distinct eGC structural remodeling compared with volume-driven crystalloid resuscitation following T/HS. These findings highlight the potential for resuscitation strategy after hemorrhagic shock to influence neurological recovery, even in the absence of direct brain injury.

articles.title: What is your diagnosis? A life-threatening complication in severe acute pancreatitis.

National Early Warning Score 2-Guided Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle Care for Adults With Suspected Sepsis in the Emergency Department: A Hybrid Type 1 Effectiveness-Implementation Stepped-Wedge Randomized Controlled Trial Pilot Study (NEWS-1 TRIPS).
articles.abstract: To increase the uptake of the Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle, we implemented a novel sepsis care model (National Early Warning Score [NEWS]-1 care), in which the Hour-1 Bundle is objectively triggered by a high NEWS-2 (≥ 5). We aimed to determine the feasibility of a full-scale type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial of this model. A pilot type 1 hybrid trial, comprising a stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial and mixed-methods implementation evaluation with staff focus group interviews and an anonymous survey guided by the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework. Four emergency departments in Hong Kong. Adult patients of 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of infection requiring hospitalization and a NEWS-2 greater than or equal to 5. Implementation of the Hour-1 Bundle when NEWS-2 was greater than or equal to 5. The primary outcome was the feasibility of a full-scale hybrid trial, evaluated based on 14 progression criteria. Preliminary clinical effectiveness and safety were assessed, alongside implementation barriers and facilitators. During the implementation phase, compliance with lactate, blood culture, and antibiotics increased significantly. All progression criteria were met, except for suboptimal overall bundle compliance (56.1%). Exploratory intention-to-treat analysis (standard care group, n = 102; NEWS-1 group, n = 98) showed no significant between-group difference in 30-day all-cause mortality (standard care group, 3.9%; NEWS-1 group, 9.2%; absolute risk difference, 5.3%; 95% CI -1.6% to 12.1%); in-hospital, 90-day all-cause, or sepsis-related mortality; need for mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, intensive care, or surgery; or ventilator-free days and adverse events. Implementation evaluation identified 15 barriers and 13 facilitators. The effectiveness of NEWS-1 care remained uncertain, though adverse events were rare. A full-scale hybrid stepped-wedge trial is feasible but requires a much larger sample size. Real-world implementation barriers and facilitators should be considered in sepsis management guidelines.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Obstetric Causes of Critical Illness in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: To determine the prevalence, risks, and outcomes of obstetric causes of critically ill pregnant women admitted to the ICU. We searched the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid, and ScienceDirect databases up to May 15, 2026. We included studies reporting primary data on critically ill pregnant and postpartum women (up to 48 d post-delivery) admitted to an ICU, with relevant obstetric risk factors and maternal outcomes. Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects model with 95% CIs. Of the 3,735 total records, 50 studies met the eligibility criteria, encompassing 7,756,232 women receiving obstetric care in tertiary hospitals across 20 countries, with 49,299 ICU admissions. Globally, 1.0% (95% CI, 0.8-1.3%) of pregnant and postpartum women experience critical illness and require admission to an ICU. The frequency varies according to the country's income levels, with the highest in low-income countries (4.1%) and the lowest in high-income countries (0.5%). Notably, 72.3% of ICU admissions were attributed to known obstetric causes, primarily obstetric hemorrhage (23.3%) and hypertension in pregnancy (26.9%). Nearly 33.3% of ICU patients required either respiratory or transfusion support, and the maternal mortality rate among ICU-admitted obstetric women was 8.5%. Nearly one in 100 pregnancies require admission to intensive care due to critical illness, and nearly three-quarters of these admissions were due to direct obstetric causes, with high maternal morbidity and mortality. Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders account for the majority of ICU admissions. Strengthening obstetric care in resource-limited settings through the expansion and optimization of intensive care services is essential for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes and reducing preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Neurological Outcomes of Rhythm Transitions in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest With Initial Nonshockable Rhythms: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the prognostic implications of rhythm transitions between asystole and pulseless electrical activity (PEA) in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients with initial nonshockable rhythms. Nationwide population-based observational study. Nationwide OHCA Registry of South Korea, managed by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency. Consecutive adult (≥ 18 yr old) OHCA patients with nonshockable rhythms from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2021. None. Patients were categorized into four groups based on rhythm changes during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR): asystole-to-asystole (A-A), asystole-to-PEA (A-P), PEA-to-asystole (P-A), and PEA-to-PEA (P-P). The primary outcome was good neurologic outcome at hospital discharge, defined as a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1-2. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for measured confounding. In the primary IPTW model, weighted risks of good neurologic outcome were 0.101% in A-A, 0.231% in A-P, 0.384% in P-A, and 0.874% in P-P. Compared with A-A, the odds of good neurologic outcome were higher in A-P (odds ratio [OR], 2.28; 95% CI, 1.78-2.93; risk difference [RD], 0.130 percentage points), P-A (OR, 3.80; 95% CI, 3.01-4.80; RD, 0.283 percentage points), and P-P (OR, 8.70; 95% CI, 6.98-10.83; RD, 0.773 percentage points). Compared with A-P, P-A had higher odds of good neurologic outcome (OR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.39-1.99; RD, 0.153 percentage points). Asystole conversion to PEA during CPR was associated with a better neurologic outcome than persistent asystole. Although transitioning from PEA to asystole was associated with lower odds of a good outcome compared with persistent PEA, it was associated with a better outcome than A-P transitions. Recognizing these patterns may provide prognostic context beyond a single rhythm assessment.

articles.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review of In-Hospital and Post-Discharge Outcomes.
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis determines the incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) in critically ill patients, risks of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism, anticoagulation therapy, and the proportion diagnosed with AF post-discharge. A search of registered databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL) was performed from inception to April 20, 2026. Eligible studies included critically ill patients (≥ 18 yr old) who developed NOAF during admission to general ICUs or high-dependency units. NOAF was defined as AF in patients without prior history of AF. Data were independently extracted from full-text versions of included studies by nonblinded reviewers. A Bayesian meta-analysis was conducted on 54 studies (367,896 patients) with a random-effects model using R (Version 4.3.3). Pooled incidence of NOAF in critically ill patients was 10.6% (95% credible interval [CrI], 8.6-12.9%). Absolute risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism was 7.1% (95% CrI, 4.5-11.0%), changing to 6.9% (95% CrI, 4.2-11.6%) after age and sex adjustment. Evidence from six studies reports that critically ill patients with NOAF had 1.94 times (95% CrI, 1.23-3.29) higher relative risk of systemic thromboembolism post-discharge than patients without NOAF, rising to 2.01 (95% CrI, 1.54-2.80) with adjustment. Absolute and relative risk are evaluated with follow-up durations ranging from 1.5 months to 5 years, with variable anticoagulation exposure. Anticoagulation rates were low: 32.9% in-hospital (95% CrI, 14.6-57.9%) and 35.9% post-discharge (95% CrI, 19.7-55.9%). On follow-up, 23.9% (95% CrI, 13.9-38.5%) of critically ill patients with NOAF were subsequently diagnosed with AF. Our review suggests that NOAF during critical illness is associated with significantly increased risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism and subsequent AF diagnosis. However, rates of anticoagulation initiation remain low, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and targeted strategies post-discharge.

articles.title: Structured Patient and Family-Centered Rounding in the ICU is Associated With Increased Family Confidence in Staff Compassion and Perceived Quality of Information Shared.
articles.abstract: Determine whether inviting families to participate in structured, multidisciplinary rounding in the ICU can lead to improved quality of information shared and greater overall confidence in the care delivered to patients. Pre- and postimplementation observational study based on surveys provided by the Society of Critical Care Medicine-Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute initiative. Academic teaching hospital with 21 medical (closed unit) and 25 surgical (open unit) ICU beds. Family members and care providers of critically ill adults of 18 years and older. Families and clinicians were surveyed before and after implementation of a quality initiative to promote greater patient and family-centeredness in daily ICU rounds, using a structured and scripted rounding template. Additional information was gathered regarding provider attitudes toward the incorporation of families in rounds. In pre-and postintervention periods, 36 and 28 families were surveyed in the MICU, and 44 and 42 families were surveyed in the SICU, respectively. In pre-and postintervention periods, respectively, 53 and 48 clinicians were surveyed in the MICU, and 46 and 28 clinicians were surveyed in the SICU. Clinician perceptions improved favorably in the MICU, with statistically significant improvements falling under the category of family welcoming, presence, and participation in decision-making; less so in the SICU. Family perceptions improved in almost all parameters in the MICU, with statistical significance achieved in perceived interest in patient needs, control of agitation and pain, and consistency and honesty of information shared. Similar patterns were observed in the SICU but did not reach statistical significance. Structured, multi-disciplinary rounding with regular inclusion of family members and bedside nurses was associated with significantly greater family confidence in the quality and honesty of information shared, and an increase in perceived compassion in the care provided by ICU staff. Clinician perceptions regarding family inclusion on rounds were generally positive.

articles.title: The Impact of Hospital Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Volume and Its Distribution Across ICUs on Adult Patients' Outcomes: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
articles.abstract: Research from a prior era of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) found that higher hospital ECMO volume was associated with higher survival rates, but it did not examine whether distributing ECMO volume across multiple ICUs affected this relationship. Retrospective analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry. ECMO centers contributing to the registry. Adult patients required ECMO support from 2012 to 2023. None. We analyzed adult patients from the ELSO registry (2012-2023), adjusting for hospital factors and case mix using multivariable hierarchical logistic regression. The main outcome was in-hospital mortality. Hospital experience was measured by the annual number of adult ECMO cases and total ECMO hours. Volume-outcome associations were modeled for all centers and by total adult ICUs per center. We included 115,849 adults on ECMO across 495 hospitals. Model estimates showed small decreases in mortality odds with higher annual case counts (odds ratio [OR], 0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99 per 10-case increase) and ECMO hours (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr increase). Hospitals with one ICU had a median of 10 cases (interquartile interval [IQI], 3-25 cases), while those with four or more ICUs had a median of 50 (IQI, 28-91). Adjusted mortality was higher in centers delivering ECMO across four+ ICUs compared with one ICU (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.06-1.31), the annual case model (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06-1.26), and the annual ECMO hours model. Higher volume was associated with a reduction in the odds of mortality for hospitals with four+ ICUs compared with those with one ICU (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.96-1.00 per 10 cases and OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr). Higher hospital ECMO volume is associated with reduced mortality. Hospitals with more adult ICUs that perform ECMO may experience higher mortality, which may be explained by increased patient complexity and is offset by the higher center volume. More research is needed to better understand the optimum design of ECMO centers.

articles.title: A Telemedicine Intervention for Spontaneous Awakening and Breathing Trials in Small and Large ICUs.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the effect of a tele-critical care (TCC) daily audit-and-feedback intervention on spontaneous awakening trial and spontaneous breathing trial protocol compliance. Pre-post quality improvement study. Single health system composed of 14 hospitals in the Midwestern United States. A total of 8909 patients of 18 years or older receiving mechanical ventilation via endotracheal tube for more than 1 calendar day between October 01, 2022 and September 20, 2024. Daily in the early afternoon, TCC nurses reviewed mechanically ventilated patients to determine whether a spontaneous awakening trial and spontaneous breathing trial had occurred. They contacted the bedside nurse if no trial had occurred and no weaning exclusion criteria were noted during a manual chart review. The coprimary outcomes were the proportion of ventilator days during each ventilator episode with documentation of spontaneous awakening trials and spontaneous breathing trials. Linear mixed effects models were used to examine the effect of the intervention on each outcome stratified by ICU size (large ≥ 15 beds or small < 15 beds). Spontaneous awakening trial documentation improved over time throughout the entire period, but the rate of improvement increased significantly after the telemedicine intervention (preintervention slope: 0.2% increase per 30 d; 95% CI, -0.2% to 0.6% and postintervention slope: 1.4% increase per 30 d; 95% CI, 1.0% to 1.9%; p < 0.001 for intervention-time interaction). The telemedicine intervention was associated with a step increase in spontaneous breathing trial documentation in small ICUs (absolute increase, 12.8%; 95% CI, 8.7-16.9%) but not in large ICUs (absolute increase, -0.1%; 95% CI, -1.8% to 1.6%; p = 0.02 for intervention-ICU size interaction). The telemedicine intervention was associated with increased spontaneous awakening trials and spontaneous breathing trials selectively in small ICUs. Telemedicine may have promoted practice standardization in small ICUs where exposure to ventilated patients was infrequent. Local ICU characteristics may impact the effectiveness of TCC interventions.

articles.title: Rapid molecular diagnostics for VAP: unresolved questions and directions for future research.
GUT-LIVER CROSSTALK: A NOVEL CD226-CD112 INHIBITOR PREVENTS GUT-PRIMED NETOSIS AND ATTENUATES ACUTE LIVER INJURY IN SEPSIS.
articles.abstract: We recently identified a novel interaction between intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) and neutrophils via CD226 and CD112. This interaction induces neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and promotes inflammatory gut-liver crosstalk in sepsis. By mapping the binding site between CD112 and CD226, DPX2 was created to inhibit IEL-induced NET formation. We hypothesize that DPX2 treatment inhibits IEL-mediated NETosis and the subsequent pathologic gut-liver crosstalk. Adult C57BL/6 mice were subjected to sepsis by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). The treatment group received a 1 μg/g BW i.p. injection of DPX2, while the control group received PBS as vehicle. Liver tissue was evaluated for pro-inflammatory markers, myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity, and TUNEL staining. Serum was analyzed for liver enzyme and cytokine levels. A 7-day survival study was also conducted. NETs in the portal vein blood and MPO in the liver were increased in septic mice but were significantly reduced by DPX2. Liver tissue levels of inflammatory markers were increased in vehicle-treated septic mice, whereas these parameters were significantly decreased in the DPX2 group. TUNEL staining as well as transaminase levels revealed significant elevations in the vehicle group with significant reduction in hepatocyte injury/death with DPX2. Systemic inflammatory markers were significantly increased in the vehicle group but were significantly decreased in the DPX2 group. Lastly, there was a significant improvement in survival in the DPX2 group compared to the vehicle group. Treatment with DPX2 reduces NETosis, acute liver injury, and systemic inflammatory response, leading to improved survival in sepsis.

articles.title: Optimizing aztreonam/ceftazidime-avibactam for difficult-to-treat Stenotrophomonas maltophilia pneumonia: the importance of continuous infusion and therapeutic drug monitoring.
Cardioversion and stroke volume index rather than heart rate alone define haemodynamic success of rate control in septic shock-associated atrial fibrillation.
Pragmatic Clinical indicators of Tuberculosis Transmission Risk: a Household Contact Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions. Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB? We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates. Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk. Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.

articles.title: Associations between temperatures, extreme temperature events, and onset of acute exacerbations of COPD: a time-stratified case-crossover study in China.
articles.abstract: Non-optimal temperatures and extreme temperature events may trigger acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD), but most evidence is admission based, potentially misclassifying exposure timing and obscuring susceptible groups. Are non-optimal temperature and extreme temperature events associated with AECOPD onset, and which patients are most susceptible? We used the Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Registry (ACURE) data and assigned residential temperature exposure using ERA5-Land, a reanalysis dataset of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Cold spells (CS) were defined as consecutive days below location-specific low-temperature thresholds, and compound cold spells (CCS) as concurrent daytime and nighttime cold spells. Associations with reported symptom onset were estimated using a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional logistic regression with distributed lag nonlinear models. Subgroup and cytokine analyses assessed susceptibility and inflammation. Among 5,634 patients with AECOPD (mean age, 69.4 ± 9.5 years; 78.8% male), lower temperature was associated with higher odds of AECOPD onset, whereas higher temperature was not. The strongest associations occurred for CS lasting ≥3 days and CCS lasting ≥2 days over lag 0-3 days, with ORs of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.22-2.78) and 4.31 (95% CI, 2.07-8.97), respectively. Nearly half had delayed admission within 14 days. Using admission rather than onset dates attenuated estimates by 88.8% for CS and 84.8% for CCS. Associations were stronger among older adults, men, smokers, patients with severe AECOPD in the past year or previously diagnosed COPD, and those using combination inhaler in the preceding year. CS were also associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL-11 concentrations. Lower temperature and extreme cold events, particularly CCS, were associated with AECOPD onset. Symptom-onset timing may better capture temperature-related associations than admission timing. These findings highlight the need for targeted cold-weather prevention strategies to reduce AECOPD burden. ClinicalTrials.gov; NO.: NCT02657525.

articles.title: Beyond barriers: Understanding delays before bystander CPR as a dynamic process.
Learning at the bedside is not the same as reaching it.
Characterization of Urgent ICU Consultations in the Evaluation of Processes of Care and the Outcomes of Children in Hospital (EPOCH) Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Evaluation of Processes of Care and the Outcomes of Children in Hospital (EPOCH) Investigators
articles.abstract: Urgent ICU consultation is intended to elicit advice and consider ICU transfer. Our objective was to describe the nature and outcomes of ICU consultations across a global cohort. This is a secondary analysis of patients with one or more ICU consultations. A care episode was defined as consecutive urgent ICU consultations until an ICU admission or at least 2 weeks without an urgent ICU consultation. We describe consultation outcomes for the last care episode. Late escalations were defined by a Children's Resuscitation Intensity Scale score greater than 2. Twenty-one centers participating in the Evaluation of Processes of Care and the Outcomes of Children in Hospital (EPOCH) cluster-randomized trial. There were 4288 urgent ICU consultations in 3625 care episodes for 3000 patients with a median (interquartile range) age of 25 months (5-99 mo). In the parent EPOCH trial, hospitals were randomized to Bedside Pediatric Early Warning System or usual care; no intervention was assigned in this secondary analysis. The outcomes of the 3000 last care episodes were in-consultation death in three (0.1%) and urgent ICU admission in 1477 (49.2%). Among 3000 first, 400 second, and 68 third consultations, the proportions of ICU admission were 42%, 44%, and 47%. The proportions of ICU admissions that were late escalation were similar across groups: 18% for first and second urgent ICU consultations, and 25% for third urgent ICU consultations. among patients having a second urgent ICU consultation, patients who had received resuscitation interventions in their first urgent ICU consultation (and remained on the ward) had more frequent resuscitation events (23.2% vs. 3.4%, p < 0.01) and had a similar frequency of late escalation (31.8% vs. 15.6%, p = 0.07) and ICU admission (51.1% vs. 43.1%, p = 0.40) compared with patients without resuscitation in their first urgent ICU consultation. Urgent consultation to the ICU is common during pediatric hospitalization. Repeated ICU consultation was associated with a similar frequency of late escalation. Resuscitation measures were provided in one of 12 ICU consultations where patients were not admitted to ICU and were a risk factor for late escalation in subsequent consultations.

articles.title: Low Physical Activity and Reported Barriers Among Survivors of Critical Illness: A Mixed-Method Study.
authors: Trajectories of Recovery after ACutE and cRitical illness (TRACER) study group
articles.abstract: To examine physical activity levels in survivors of critical illness across 6 months, and to understand the barriers and facilitators of physical activity. Prospective, longitudinal, convergent mixed-methods study. Functional testing laboratory. Adults admitted to the ICU for at least 72 hours with acute respiratory failure or sepsis. None. Patients wore an accelerometer starting at hospital discharge, at 3- and 6-month follow-up to quantify daily step counts. At 6 months, physical function and patient-reported outcomes were collected in-person, with a subset of participants completing semi-structured interviews. Eighty-two patients were enrolled, with 67 (82%) having physical activity data with median age of 60 years (interquartile range [IQR], 52-66 yr), 54% male, and ICU stay 9.0 days [IQR, 5.8-17.0 d]. The median daily steps were 1358 (IQR, 742-2799) in 50 patients at baseline, 2305 (IQR, 1081-3898) in 54 patients at 3 months, and 2826 (IQR, 1609-4781) in 44 patients at 6 months. Higher comorbidity burden and earlier measurement associated with lower step counts. At 6 months, patients walked a mean of 344 ± 169 meters on the 6-minute walk test and reported being sedentary a median of 300 min/days (150-480 min/d). Eleven participants completed interviews, yielding three themes: 1) "a marathon, not a sprint": the extended ICU recovery trajectory; 2) engagement in physical activity is highly regulated by personal context; 3) value-driven and motivation-informed physical activity decisions. Mixed-methods integration demonstrated that qualitative themes expanded upon quantitative findings to explain nonlinear recovery patterns, contextualizing persistent sedentary behavior, and revealing that motivational and behavioral gaps are not captured by accelerometry. Survivors showed gradual improvement in daily steps over 6 months yet remained below recommended activity levels. Survivorship and attrition biases may lead to overestimation of step counts, further warranting larger studies. Integrating quantitative and qualitative data reveals modifiable contextual factors that may inform the design of pragmatic physical activity interventions.

articles.title: Evaluation of Sequential Organ Failure Assessment-2 Performance Across Demographic Subgroups: An External Validation Using MIMIC-IV.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the discrimination and calibration of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-2 score for ICU mortality across demographic subgroups defined by age, sex, race and ethnicity, primary language, and insurance status. Retrospective cohort study. Single academic medical center in the northeastern United States (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston, MA), using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV database (version 3.1), 2008-2022, a dataset external to the SOFA-2 development cohort. Adult patients (≥ 18 yr) with at least one ICU admission. The first ICU admission of the first qualifying hospitalization per patient was analyzed. None. First-day SOFA-2 scores were calculated from the worst values recorded during the first 24 hours of ICU admission across six organ systems, with ICU mortality as the primary outcome. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and calibration using intercept and slope, with subgroup differences in AUROC estimated by bootstrap resampling. Among 64,015 ICU patients (mean [sd] age, 64.6 [17.1] yr; 56.1% male; 66.1% White), overall AUROC was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.76-0.77). Discrimination declined significantly with age: AUROC, 0.85 (0.83-0.87) for ages 18-44 years vs. 0.72 (0.70-0.73) for ages 75 or older (ΔAUROC, -0.14 [95% CI, -0.16 to -0.11]), with systematic underprediction in older patients. Discrimination was significantly decreased among non-English speakers (ΔAUROC, -0.04) but did not differ across documented racial/ethnic groups. Patients with missing demographic information had markedly higher mortality than the overall cohort rate of 7.2% (14.1% for missing race/ethnicity; 23.1% for missing language). SOFA-2 demonstrated good overall performance but with clinically meaningful variation across subgroups, particularly with age and language. Patients with missing demographic data experienced markedly higher mortality. These findings argue for routine equity evaluation as a complement to traditional validation of clinical prediction tools.

articles.title: The Effect of Guanfacine on Delirium in Surgical and Trauma ICU Patients: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of conducting a randomized controlled trial investigating guanfacine for ICU delirium, including assessment of recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, and data completeness, while estimating treatment effects to inform future trial design. Single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial conducted from November 2020 to February 2023. Surgical and Trauma ICUs at the University of Alabama at Birmingham Hospital. One hundred critically ill adults with Confusion Assessment Method-ICU-confirmed delirium randomized 1:1 to guanfacine or placebo. Patients received 2 mg guanfacine or matching placebo nightly for up to 14 days, or until ICU discharge or delirium resolution. Primary feasibility outcomes included protocol adherence (target ≥ 90%), retention (target ≥ 80%), recruitment rate (target ≥ 2 patients/mo), and data completeness (target ≥ 95%). Most feasibility targets were achieved: protocol adherence was 100%, retention was 100%, and data completeness was 100%. Recruitment was significantly impacted by COVID-19 pandemic disruptions, achieving 0.9 patients/wk during active recruitment periods.For clinical outcomes, in unadjusted analyses, median delirium and coma-free days were higher with guanfacine than placebo (2 [interquartile range [IQR], 0-6] vs. 1 [IQR, 0-4]; p = 0.02); however, this association was not statistically significant after adjustment for prespecified baseline covariates. ICU and hospital length of stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ significantly between groups. No hemodynamic differences or safety concerns were observed. This pilot study successfully supports feasibility for a definitive trial, with excellent protocol adherence, adequate retention, and preliminary signals that warrant further evaluation. Although adjusted analyses were not statistically significant, the observed unadjusted difference in delirium and coma-free days and favorable safety profile support progression to a multicenter trial informed by these pilot estimates.

articles.title: Composite Endpoints in Critical Care Delirium Trials.
articles.abstract: Delirium is an abnormal mental status, commonly occurring among critically ill patients, in which a person's attention and awareness change acutely. Delirium is associated with negative outcomes, including death. Furthermore, a longer duration of delirium is associated with long-term cognitive impairment in survivors of critical illness. Hence, there is a need for novel interventions that reduce the duration of delirium; however, measuring and analyzing "duration of delirium" as an endpoint in randomized trials is challenging due to the episodic nature of delirium and the competing events of coma and death, which can bias analyses of duration of delirium. Given these challenges, delirium trials have adopted one of two composite endpoints: delirium- and coma-free days, defined as the number of days alive without delirium or coma for both survivors and nonsurvivors, and an alternative composite that ranks death as the worst state and orders days alive without delirium or coma among survivors. To date, these composite endpoints have not been rigorously evaluated. Hence, herein we use data from the Maximizing Efficacy of Targeted Sedation and Reducing Neurologic Dysfunction (MENDS) trial to motivate the use of composite endpoints in critical care delirium trials, discuss how to define the effect of treatment on each composite endpoint and their clinical interpretability, and present a method for visualizing how the treatment effects accrue over the course of follow-up. Based on these analyses, we provide practical recommendations for the use of composite endpoints in critical care delirium trials, which could be extended to other randomized trials that rely on similar composite endpoints.

articles.title: From sirens to systems: Characterizing EMS and trauma care across America.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: State emergency medical services (EMS) and trauma systems determine prehospital triage, transport, trauma center designation, data reporting, and quality improvement, yet their contemporary organization has not been systematically characterized. We sought to describe state-level EMS and trauma system structures, policies, resources, and perceived gaps across the United States. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of EMS and trauma system leaders in all 50 states and the District of Columbia from July 2025 through March 2026. A 56-item instrument utilizing categorical, Likert-type, rank-order, and free-text items assessed oversight, prehospital triage and transport, clinical protocols, trauma center verification, registries, quality improvement, and funding. Respondents were recruited by email and phone. Multiple respondents could contribute complementary domain-level information to a single state profile. Responses were summarized descriptively. All 51 jurisdictions participated. Most states reported a state EMS medical director (84%), statewide trauma triage protocols (84%), and mandatory participation in their state trauma registry (88%). However, operational coordination varied: only 29% had a centralized trauma communications center, only 6% of states reported a single point of contact for helicopter EMS dispatch, and 35% required a certificate of need for new helicopter services. Trauma center verification relied on American College of Surgeons (ACS) verification in 59% of states, while others used state-administered processes. More than half of states rated EMS financial resources in the two lowest adequacy categories, and 55% reported that their trauma system required at least moderate improvement. Rural populations were most frequently identified as underserved (96%) and as experiencing worse outcomes (92%). State EMS and trauma systems share broad adoption of national clinical standards but differ substantially in governance, coordination, verification, data integration, and funding. Level V, Prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Normocapnia Versus Mild Hypercapnia During Lung Protective Ventilation in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract: This trial emulation aimed to answer the question: Among patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) who receive lung protective ventilation with low tidal volume, is normocapnia through an increase in respiratory rate associated with lower mortality than mild hypercapnia? Target trial emulation. Hospitals of the ARDS Network and Prevention and Early Treatment of Acute Lung Injury (PETAL) Network. Patients with ARDS enrolled in seven ARDS Network and PETAL Network randomized controlled trials. None. A target trial was emulated, assigning participants in a 1:1 ratio to normocapnia (target Paco2 35-45 mm Hg) or mild hypercapnia (target Paco2 50-55 mm Hg) for 4 days following the initiation of lung protective ventilation. The primary outcome was 90-day in-hospital mortality. Of 5367 potentially eligible subjects, 292 patients were assigned to normocapnia and 292 to mild hypercapnia. Separation in Paco2 values was preserved over the 4-day period of emulated intervention. Both groups had median pH greater than or equal to 7.33. Bicarbonate levels, driving pressure, tidal volume, and dead-space fraction did not differ clinically significantly between groups, while median respiratory rate was 33.0 breaths/min in the normocapnia vs. 28.0 breaths/min in the mild hypercapnia group (p < 0.001). Death within 90 days occurred in 84 of 292 patients (28.8%) in the normocapnia group and in 84 of 292 patients (28.8%) in the mild hypercapnia group (log-rank p = 0.842). This result persisted in subgroups such as older (≥ 65 yr) and obese (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m2) patients. Among patients with ARDS who received lung protective ventilation, normocapnia through an increase in respiratory rate was not associated with lower mortality than mild hypercapnia. As this finding is derived from a trial emulation, it should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for significant residual bias.

articles.title: Circulating Cell-Free Mitochondrial DNA, Delirium, and Long-Term Cognitive Impairment in Critically Ill Adults With Sepsis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: During sepsis, circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) is released and elevated due to cell injury, augments the immune response, and may contribute to organ dysfunction. Delirium is common and deleterious during sepsis, but little is known about the relationship between mitochondrial injury and delirium during sepsis. We sought therefore to examine associations between ccf-mtDNA and delirium and other clinical outcomes during sepsis. Multicenter, prospective cohort study. Medical and surgical ICUs in university and community hospitals in Nashville, TN. Four hundred eighty patients with sepsis plus shock and/or acute respiratory failure. None. We measured ccf-mtDNA in plasma collected on multiple days (study days 1, 3, and 5) during sepsis and assessed participants bid for delirium and coma using the validated Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU and Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale. We then assessed survivors' cognitive function 3 and 12 months after hospital discharge using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status. During sepsis, the adjusted odds of delirium were 7% lower for individuals at the 75th percentile of ccf-mtDNA compared with those at the 25th percentile (odds ratio [OR], 0.93; 95% CI, 0.86-0.99; p = 0.048). ccf-mtDNA was marginally associated with in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.99-1.20; p = 0.08), but was not associated with coma (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.90-1.05; p = 0.31) or 3-month (beta, 0.23; 95% CI, -1.58 to 2.05; p = 0.80) and 12-month (beta, -0.36; 95% CI, -2.13 to 1.42; p = 0.69) cognitive outcomes. In this multicenter, prospective cohort study, higher levels of ccf-mtDNA were associated with lower odds of delirium, a result that contradicted our hypothesis. This provocative finding should be interpreted cautiously until replicated and explained by future studies.

articles.title: Alarm Fatigue Across Critical Care Domains: Comparative Insights and Independent Predictors From a Cross-Sectional Multicenter Survey Study.
articles.abstract: Alarm fatigue, the desensitization to excessive false alarms, threatens patient safety and staff performance across critical care domains. It is unclear whether alarm fatigue differs between hospital departments. This study compared alarm fatigue among staff in the ICU, cardiac telemetry ward (CTW), and operating room (OR), and, secondarily, identified its independent determinants. Cross-sectional, multicenter survey study. ICUs, a CTW, and ORs. A total of 514 healthcare professionals working in the ICU, CTW, and OR. None. Alarm fatigue was assessed using the Dutch-translated Charité Alarm Fatigue Questionnaire, which includes alarm stress and alarm coping subscales. Participants also rated their self-perceived alarm fatigue on a 1-10 scale and the percentage of perceived false alarms. Telemetry staff reported the highest self-perceived alarm fatigue (B = 0.65; 95% CI, 0.06-1.24; p = 0.032) and perceived false alarms (B = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.23-1.30; p = 0.005), while OR staff reported the lowest (B = -1.01; 95% CI, -1.59 to -0.43; p < 0.001). Second, physicians (B = -0.13; 95% CI, -0.25 to -0.01; p < 0.031) and less experienced staff (< 3 mo; B = -0.34; 95% CI, -0.68 to -0.01; p = 0.046) reported lower alarm fatigue. Alarm fatigue varied significantly across departments and professions, being highest in telemetry staff and lowest among physicians and less experienced personnel. Targeted department-specific interventions and longitudinal research are necessary to mitigate alarm fatigue and enhance patient safety.

Efficacy and safety of oliceridine versus remifentanil for analgesia in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (CO-ROAM): a multicenter, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Remifentanil provides effective analgesia during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but its utility is limited by opioid-related adverse events. Oliceridine, a G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, may decouple analgesia from these effects, but lacks evidence in critically ill patients. This multicentre, assessor- and patient-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial was conducted across 19 intensive care units (ICUs) in China. Adults receiving IMV were randomised 1:1 to oliceridine or remifentanil, titrated to a Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool score below 3. The primary endpoint was time in target analgesic range (TTR; non-inferiority margin -10%). Of 307 randomised patients, 304 comprised the modified intention-to-treat population (151 oliceridine, 153 remifentanil). Median TTR was 96.0% versus 92.3% (absolute difference 3.7%, 95% CI -0.3-5.7%). Oliceridine was associated with fewer mild-to-moderate adverse drug reactions (ADRs), occurring at 15.9 versus 22.2 events per 100 patient-days (IRR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, P = 0.049), and a lower rate of respiratory depression during the study period (0% vs. 4.6%, P = 0.015). Post-extubation respiratory depression (0% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.005) and analgesic-sedation costs were both lower with oliceridine. IMV duration, ICU stay, and 28-day mortality did not differ. Subgroup analyses identified a nominal ADR benefit in patients with Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II > 17 and a larger nominal TTR difference in those without acute respiratory distress syndrome. Oliceridine provides non-inferior analgesia to remifentanil with a more favourable respiratory safety profile and lower costs in critically ill adults. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06454292 (registered June 11, 2024).

articles.title: Violent Reinjury Trajectories Across Injury Mechanisms: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Survivors of violent injury often experience reinjury. We sought to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with violent reinjury across different injury types. We conducted an observational cohort study of individuals with violent injury (ie, blunt assaults, stabbings, and firearm injuries) across 2 adult and 2 pediatric Level I trauma centers from 2016 to 2023. Covariates included age, sex, race, hospital type, insurance status, and social vulnerability. Our primary outcome was time to reinjury. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to measure associations between each covariate and time to reinjury across injury types. There were 29,038 individuals with nonfatal violent injuries. Male sex (n=19,273; 66.4%), Black and other race (n=21,403; 73.7%), presentation to adult hospitals (n=24,200; 83.3%), public insurance (n=13,879; 47.8%), and living in an area with high social vulnerability (n=21,044; 72.5%) were associated with a greater risk of any violent reinjury, adjusting for covariates. For index firearm injuries, patients younger than18 years had greater risk of firearm reinjury than patients aged 18 to 26 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]:0.65 [0.47 to 0.91]) and for those older than 26 years (aHR:0.47 [0.34 to 0.66]). Although women with firearm injury had a lower risk of firearm reinjury compared with men (aHR:0.46 [0.36 to 0.58]), they had greater risk of blunt reinjury (aHR:1.77 [1.34 to 1.24]). Patients living in areas with high social vulnerability had a higher risk of escalating reinjury mechanism (eg, blunt to firearm; aHR:1.46 [1.11 to 1.90]) versus patients in areas with low/average social vulnerability. This research underscores how sequelae of violent reinjury are shaped by certain demographic and clinical characteristics, highlighting opportunities to strengthen reinjury prevention in key subgroups.

articles.title: Unintended Exposure to Medical Aid in Dying Drug Mixtures: Principles of Emergency Care.
articles.abstract: Medical Aid in Dying (MAID) is a legal medical option for terminally ill patients with decision-making capacity to self-administer prescription medication to cause death. MAID has expanded across the United States, with New York becoming the most recent state to legalize it in August 2026. As these medications become more available in the community, typically administered outside controlled medical settings, such as the home, rare but consequential unintended exposures can occur. MAID is distinct from euthanasia in that the patient must have decision-making capacity and must be able to self-administer the medication; this requirement contributes to the presence of highly lethal drug mixtures in nonclinical environments. Although MAID formulations are designed to be lethal, unintended recipients may ingest only a partial dose (eg, a "sip"), making survival possible with prompt medical care. We review the background and common components of MAID mixtures, which typically combine a sedative (benzodiazepine and/or barbiturate), an opioid, and cardiotoxic agents such as digoxin, β-blockers, and/or tricyclic antidepressants. We propose preliminary management guidelines for suspected unsanctioned MAID exposures: early regional poison center consultation; supportive resuscitation; activated charcoal when safe; targeted diagnostics, including serum digoxin concentration and serial electrocardiograms; gastric aspiration, when feasible; use of digoxin immune Fab when indicated; avoidance of flumazenil and naloxone in mixed ingestions; and substance-specific therapies, such as high-dose insulin for propranolol toxicity and sodium bicarbonate for tricyclic antidepressants-induced QRS widening.

articles.title: The Post-Sepsis Neutrophil: Lymphocyte Ratio: A Population Signal in Search of Individual Meaning.
Association Between the Neutrophil:Lymphocyte Ratio After Hospitalization for Sepsis and Long-Term Outcomes: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Long-term outcomes after sepsis survival remain poor. No clinical laboratory tests are in use for stratifying long-term risk after sepsis, limiting the development of secondary prevention. The peripheral blood neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio (NLR) reflects innate and adaptive immune cell balance, and may reflect an immune milieu which is associated with long-term risk after sepsis. Accordingly, we evaluated the association between the NLR in the weeks after sepsis hospitalization discharge-a time when patients are routinely seen in post-ICU clinics-and long-term outcomes. Population-based cohort study. Ontario, Canada, 2010-2020. Adults discharged alive from a sepsis hospitalization. None. The exposure was the first outpatient NLR-derived from the complete blood count-measured 15-90 days after sepsis discharge. Among 37,250 survivors with available NLR, the median (interquartile range [IQR]) time-to-measurement was 34 days (22-54 d), and the median NLR was 2.7 (1.8-4.2). Within 1 year, 17,732 patients (47.6%) were rehospitalized or died (median [IQR] time-to-event, 82 d [27-185 d]). The frequency of rehospitalization or death increased across increasing NLR quartiles: 34.2%, 41.5%, 50.3%, and 64.4% (ptrend < 0.001). Compared with the lowest quartile, adjusted hazard ratios (95% CI) were 1.24 (1.18-1.29), 1.54 (1.48-1.62), and 2.25 (2.15-2.35) across higher quartiles. For most patients, NLR after sepsis returned to its patient-specific presepsis ambient level, which was itself prognostic. Among sepsis survivors, outpatient NLR measured 15-90 days after discharge is strongly associated with 1-year risk of rehospitalization or death. As a simple, widely available biomarker, the NLR may support early postsepsis risk stratification and inform development of secondary prevention strategies.

articles.title: [Communication in the resuscitation room: a core element of crew resource management (CRM) for safe patient care : Current developments, practical examples, and key information for resuscitation room training].
articles.abstract: The care of critically ill patients in the resuscitation room is generally provided by a multi-professional and interdisciplinary resuscitation team. Current developments among institutions that set the framework for healthcare underscore that effective communication and targeted team training must be understood not as supplementary measures, but rather as fundamental to successful patient care. For example, the German Association for Emergency Medicine (DGINA) considers qualifications in team leadership and crew resource management (CRM) for medical and nursing team members in the care of critically ill, non-traumatological patients to be indispensable. Secure and effective communication is one of these qualifications and is regarded as a central element of the five non-technical skills. The role of non-technical skills and the CRM training built upon them in preventing errors related to "human factors" has increasingly gained recognition in the medical community in recent years. Despite convincing literature, there are still no legal regulations in Germany at present stipulating the content, structure, or implementation of regular CRM (resuscitation room) training.

articles.title: [Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) : Consensus statement of the DGK, DGTHG, DGAI, DGPTM, DIVI, GRC, DRG, ALKK and DGIIN].
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) can be considered as a rescue strategy in highly selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest and a potentially reversible cause of cardiac arrest. Both ECPR itself and the subsequent treatment under extracorporeal life support (ECLS) are complex and resource intensive. There is currently no robust evidence for the superiority of ECPR over conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation. The implementation and maintenance of an effective ECPR program requires clearly structured processes, defined communication channels and robust institutional infrastructure for quality assurance. Ensuring comprehensive and intersectoral quality of care requires the cooperative collaboration of many necessary disciplines. This consensus paper updates the document published in 2018 and defines a common framework of central structural, procedural and clinical requirements.

Trends in Care and Outcomes Among Emergency Department Patients With Chest Pain Without Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract: To characterize trends in hospitalization, downstream care, and outcomes among emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain without acute myocardial infarction (AMI) diagnosis. We analyzed claims data from a large national commercial insurer (2007-2021) and identified ED visits with a principal diagnosis of chest pain. We excluded visits with secondary diagnoses of AMI or other significant cardiopulmonary conditions and those preceded by cardiac testing, coronary procedures, AMI admissions, or chest pain ED visits within 6 months. Usage outcomes included index hospitalization (principal), 7-day cardiac testing, and 30-day coronary revascularization. The principal clinical outcome was 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization. Adjusted annual rates were estimated using generalized estimating equations, and trends were assessed using inverse-variance-weighted linear regression. We included 773,250 index chest pain ED visits (mean age 54.2 years; 54.3% women). Adjusted hospitalization rates declined from 42.7% to 18.6%, and 7-day noninvasive testing decreased from 26.7% to 9.1%. Revascularization within 30 days declined from 5.8% to 3.6%. Overall, 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization showed no significant temporal trend, ranging from 0.8% to 1.2%. However, a modest increasing trend was observed among patients aged 70 years and older. Among ED patients with chest pain without AMI diagnosis, hospitalization, cardiac testing, and revascularization declined substantially from 2007 to 2021. Overall, downstream AMI hospitalization remained stable, although those in older adults experienced modest rises. Although efforts continue to identify additional low-risk patients for safe discharge, future research should quantify the potential benefits of hospitalization and cardiac testing, particularly for older adults and high-risk patients.

articles.title: Concepts in Practice: Understanding and Addressing Name-Based Microaggressions in Health Care.
articles.abstract: Names are important markers of identity, culture, and belonging. In health care settings, individuals with ethnically distinct names may experience repeated mispronunciations, unsolicited nicknames, or avoidance of their names. Repeated mispronunciations without sincere efforts to learn or improve, as well as the avoidance, dismissal, or replacement of names with unsolicited nicknames, may function as name-based microaggressions and can negatively affect psychological safety, professional identity formation, and workplace inclusion. In this manuscript, we discuss the effect of name-based microaggressions on health care professionals and trainees, with particular focus on the emergency department. We review the 3 major categories of microaggressions-microassaults, microinsults, and microinvalidations-and use clinical vignettes to demonstrate how these behaviors may appear in both interpersonal and institutional settings. We also propose practical interpersonal and institutional strategies to promote more inclusive workplaces and foster respectful engagement with ethnically distinct names. By encouraging greater awareness, curiosity, humility, and intentionality around names, health care organizations can help cultivate clinical environments where individuals feel respected, included, and valued.

Live Versus Delayed Video-Based TEAM Assessment During Real-World Cardiac Arrest: Agreement and Exploratory Differences by Rater Experience.
articles.abstract: To evaluate agreement between immediate live and delayed video-based assessment of nontechnical skills during real-world adult cardiac arrest resuscitation, and whether agreement differed by rater experience. We conducted a prospective observational study of adult cardiac arrest resuscitations in a tertiary emergency department in Taiwan in 2024. For each event, one trained physician or nurse who participated in the resuscitation completed the Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) immediately afterward and re-rated the same event from video approximately 30 days later. Live-video agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Of 105 recorded resuscitations, 80 had complete paired assessments. Mean global ratings were similar between modalities (8.25 versus 8.22; mean paired difference, -0.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.25 to 0.20), whereas teamwork scores were modestly lower on video review (mean paired difference, -1.00; 95% CI -1.77 to -0.23). Event-level agreement was limited: intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.21 (95% CI 0.00 to 0.41) for total TEAM score and 0.16 (95% CI -0.06 to 0.37) for global rating. Total TEAM video ratings averaged 1.24 points lower than live ratings, with limits of agreement from -12.28 to 9.80. Agreement was higher among senior raters. Delayed video-based TEAM assessment produced similar group-level scores but limited event-level agreement during real-world cardiac arrest. Agreement appeared higher among senior raters. Video review may support debriefing and monitoring, but appraisal of a specific resuscitation or other higher stakes use likely requires experienced raters and structured safeguards.

Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial.
articles.abstract: Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking. In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality? In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay. Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009). In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings. Calculating trauma undertriage rates: Are we using the wrong formula-and the wrong definition?
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Undertriage (UT) is central to trauma center quality improvement, yet UT definitions vary, and no data-driven consensus target exists for interfacility benchmarking. We compared facility-level UT rates across four methods and assessed the impact on facility benchmarking. This retrospective study included patients aged 18 to 89 from Level I & II trauma centers in the ACS TQP Files (2021-2023). Facility-level UT was calculated using the Cribari Matrix Method (CMM), modified Cribari Matrix Method (mCMM), Standardized Triage Assessment Tool (STAT), and High-Intensity Time-Sensitive (HITS) intervention-based definition representing trauma team actions. Paired facility-level UT rates were compared across methods. To estimate benchmarking impact, we calculated within-facility rank change (higher rank = higher UT) relative to CMM. 2,643,881 patients and 515 facilities were included. Median facility-level UT significantly differed by method: CMM 11% [interquartile range: 9-14], mCMM 60% [50-67], STAT 6% [5-8], and HITS 30% [22-40] (all P<0.001). At individual hospitals, the median range of maximum UT values between methods was 53% [44-60]. The median absolute facility rank change between the CMM method and other tools was 129 [54.5-236.5] for mCMM, 48 [17-90] for STAT, and 142 [62.5-252.5] for HITS. These UT data highlight a concerning level of variation and uncertainty in the calculation and interpretation of a key trauma center performance metric. Until a UT definition is standardized and data-driven UT target goals established, cross-center benchmarking using UT should be interpreted cautiously and may be better suited for within-center trending.
