articles.title: Pooled prevalence of infectious diseases among first responders in the prehospital setting: A systematic review with meta-analysis by occupation.
articles.abstract: First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers. Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², τ², and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool. Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p = 0.039. Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

articles.title: Emergency Response and Patient Transport in Remote Indigenous Communities: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Prehospital and inter-facility transport, such as air medical retrieval and pre-birth evacuation, often move Indigenous patients in rural and remote settings out of their communities, where care is already shaped by fragmented funding and structural inequities; no review has mapped these pathways globally. This scoping review mapped evidence on prehospital emergency response and patient transport for this population. A librarian-assisted PubMed, Embase, and Scopus search was conducted for English-language publications on March 9, 2026. Eligible studies included an explicit rural Indigenous population with a defined prehospital pathway. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed full texts, and a third reviewer resolved disagreements. Data were charted using a standardized form and synthesized descriptively. Across eight countries, 76 studies met the inclusion criteria, primarily from Australia (n = 29) and Canada (n = 23). Air transport and medical evacuation was the most frequently described pathway (71%), followed by ground transport (51%). Explicit description of paramedic or emergency medical services (24%) and dispatch/9-1-1 (12%) were depicted less frequently. Additionally, pathways were commonly described but rarely evaluated: only 12/76 (16%) publications used an evaluative design, and no pathway was evaluated in more than 7 of 76 publications (9%). The most reported barriers were infrastructure and communications (92%), cost and jurisdiction (87%), and distance to definitive care (83%). All percentages describe how often a topic was reported across the 76 included publications, and not its prevalence in practice. An explicit cultural-safety framework was applied in 9% of the publications, and community-led governance of the research in 7%. The published evidence disproportionately described transporting patients out of their communities. Community first response and tele-support were described more often than their standing in the literature suggests; however, they were rarely evaluated, and Indigenous-led governance of the research itself was reported in 7% of publications. Low reporting frequency does not establish that these models are uncommon in application and practice. Future priorities include community-partnered evaluation of community-based capacity and telehealth-supported care, alongside the development of patient and family cultural safety.

articles.title: [Emergency medicine requirements for the resuscitation room and the resuscitation room team].
articles.abstract: The resuscitation room is the central interface between prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) and in-hospital emergency care for critically ill and severely injured patients. From an EMS perspective, requirements are defined for activation, prenotification, team structure, handover, overload management and feedback. Written activation and allocation criteria are required that are applicable in the prehospital setting and agreed upon by hospitals, emergency dispatch centres and EMS providers. Prenotification must take place through a continuously available, reliable communication channel, be actively acknowledged and enable transparent feedback on capacity. Paramedics must be authorised to activate the resuscitation room independently of the presence of an emergency physician. On arrival, a qualified and operational team with clearly identifiable roles should be available. Handover should be structured and as interruption-free as possible. The exploratory online survey showed that trauma resuscitation care is predominantly guideline-based and more often includes a written minimum staffing requirement. In nontrauma resuscitation care, written activation criteria and binding team structures were less frequently available. Although handovers were mostly standardised, substantial deficits existed in overload and diversion protocols as well as in interprofessional feedback structures involving EMS. These findings indicate a need for coordinated procedures, transparent capacity management and binding quality-assurance measures.

articles.title: Effect of airway assistant training on intubation time during simulated prehospital airway management: A pilot study.
articles.abstract: Challenging airways are common in the out-of-hospital setting, where delays or failure to secure the airway can result in significant morbidity and mortality. Therefore, this pilot study aimed to determine whether training paramedics in the role of airway assistant improves intubation time during a simulated regurgitating airway using suction-assisted laryngoscopy and airway decontamination (SALAD). Twelve qualified paramedics were randomly allocated to one of two groups (n = 6) and paired with intensive care paramedics (ICPs). Airway assistants in Group 1 completed a one-hour airway assistant training program, whereas airway assistants in Group 2 received no training. Participants completed a standardized, timed simulation using a continuously regurgitating mannequin designed to replicate the challenges of out-of-hospital intubation. The primary outcome was time to successful intubation, defined as passage of the endotracheal tube through the vocal cords with cuff inflation. Airway assistant training significantly reduced intubation time. The untrained group recorded a median intubation time of 102.5 seconds (IQR 36), compared with 53 seconds (IQR 19) in the trained group. Group comparisons demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in intubation time (p = 0.009) and corresponded to a very large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.86; Hedges' g = 1.72). No association was observed between intubation time and the age or experience of either the airway assistant or the ICP. No esophageal intubations occurred in either group. In this pilot study, training paramedics to perform the airway assistant role significantly reduced intubation time in a simulated regurgitating airway. These preliminary findings suggest that incorporating structured airway assistant training into prehospital education programs may improve airway management performance in challenging environments. Given the small sample size and simulated setting, larger studies are required to confirm these findings and determine whether the observed benefits translate to clinical practice.

articles.title: Non-cardiac comorbidities and functional impairment in acute heart failure: a hospital-wide real-world cohort study (COMPACT-HF).
articles.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) is a leading cause of hospitalization among older adults and is associated with non-cardiac comorbidities (NCCs) and functional impairment. Their prognostic and therapeutic implications remain incompletely characterized. COMPACT-HF was a retrospective cohort study of adults discharged after hospitalization for AHF at a tertiary teaching hospital in 2023. Comorbidity burden was assessed using the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) and predefined NCCs. Functional impairment was defined as loss of ≥ 1 basic activity of daily living (ADL). Primary outcome was 12-month all-cause mortality. We included 456 patients (mean age 82.6 ± 8.6 years; 50% male); 96% had ≥ 1 NCC and 48% had functional impairment. Twelve-month mortality was 31%. CCI was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.17 per point; 95% CI 1.07-1.27, p < 0.001), while functional impairment provided additional prognostic information beyond comorbidity burden. Advanced chronic kidney disease, dementia, and active malignancy were among the NCCs most strongly associated with mortality. Among patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, dementia, advanced chronic kidney disease, chronic lung disease, and functional impairment were associated with lower prescription of ≥ 3 of 4 guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) classes, whereas CCI was not; GDMT prescription also varied substantially according to discharge ward. In this hospital-wide real-world cohort of patients discharged alive after AHF hospitalization, NCCs and functional impairment were highly prevalent and associated with mortality, while specific clinical conditions and discharge ward were associated with GDMT implementation. Integrating comorbidity and functional assessment may improve risk stratification and support a holistic approach to AHF management.

articles.title: Comparison of automated and manual oxygen titration in emergency care: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Supplemental oxygen is a cornerstone of emergency care but has a narrow therapeutic window, with both hypoxemia and hyperoxia associated with adverse outcomes. Despite guideline-recommended oxygen saturation targets, manual oxygen titration in acute care settings is frequently inaccurate due to human, system, and workflow limitations. Automated closed-loop oxygen titration systems, which continuously adjust oxygen delivery to maintain predefined saturation targets, have emerged as a potential solution. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of automated oxygen titration compared with standard manual titration in adult emergency care. The study protocol was registered with the international prospective register of systematic reviews (PROSPERO). A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies involving adult patients receiving emergency care were identified, with full-text review and data extraction performed in accordance with the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Twenty-two records were identified; four met inclusion criteria, including three randomized controlled trials (n = 286) and one prospective observational study. In the meta-analysis, automated titration significantly increased time within oxygen saturation target ranges compared to manual care (mean difference 22.9%; 95% CI 9.6-36.2). While initial heterogeneity was high (I2 = 85.7%), sensitivity analysis excluding one high-performing manual cohort eliminated variance (I2 = 0%) and confirmed a robust treatment effect (mean difference 29.6%; 95% CI 23.7-35.6). The available data are limited to these surrogate physiological endpoints; evidence demonstrating improvements in patient-centered clinical outcomes remains absent. Automated closed-loop titration demonstrates superior physiological precision in oxygen saturation target maintenance compared to manual care in emergency settings. While it effectively minimizes exposure to hypoxaemia and hyperoxia extremes, further large-scale trials are required to determine if these physiological improvements translate into definitive clinical benefits or improved patient-oriented outcomes.

articles.title: Estimating Dehydration Survival Limits from Plausible Mortality Thresholds.
articles.abstract: The limits of human survival during dehydration are not well defined and are infrequently based on physiological endpoints. We evaluated dehydration survivability using thresholds for hypernatremia and hypovolemia that are consistent with known mechanisms of mortality.MethodsA mass balance approach was used to model changes in blood sodium concentration and blood volume in a 75 kg adult with total body water of 43.7 L. Dehydration was scaled at a 10% loss of body mass (7.5 L). Water and electrolyte losses were modeled under conditions of sweating in warm (∼32 °C) and cool (∼4 °C) environments and during gastrointestinal illness. Blood sodium and blood volume responses were calculated based on volume-weighted sodium losses and standard compartmental assumptions.ResultsThe time to reach 10% dehydration ranged from 2.5 days (eccrine warm) to 5.9 days (eccrine cool) and 3.0 days with gastrointestinal losses. Blood sodium increased to 160 mmol·L-1 with sweating and 146 mmol·L-1 with gastrointestinal losses. Estimated blood volume reductions were 0.844 (sweating) and 1.327 L (gastrointestinal). These values reach or approach those associated with fatal hypernatremia and circulatory shock.DiscussionA dehydration level of approximately 10% body mass (17% total body water) produces physiological conditions consistent with mortality from both hypernatremia and hypovolemia. Survival without water is therefore likely limited to approximately 3 to 6 days under passive conditions, depending on environmental exposure, fluid loss pathways, and individual variability.ConclusionsHypernatremia and hypovolemia provide physiologically grounded thresholds for estimating dehydration survivability. These findings refine existing survival estimates and highlight the critical importance of minimizing fluid loss in austere environments.

articles.title: The Impact of Lifestyle Interventions and Mental Health Management on Arrhythmias in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: To summarise contemporary evidence on the impact of lifestyle interventions and mental health management on arrhythmias in patients with heart failure (HF), and to highlight emerging therapeutic opportunities. Lifestyle modification targets shared risk factors in both arrhythmias and HF. In atrial fibrillation (AF), weight loss, exercise, alcohol reduction, and risk factor management reduce arrhythmia burden and improve arrhythmia-related symptoms and quality of life. Similarly, in both HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), exercise training improves functional capacity and quality of life, whilst dietary interventions and weight loss are particularly beneficial in HFpEF. Mental health disorders represent novel targets for intervention for arrhythmias in HF; these conditions are common in arrhythmia and HF patients and associated with poorer outcomes, but early data suggests that mental health interventions do not reduce arrhythmia burden or cardiovascular outcomes despite improving overall psychological well-being and quality of life. Lifestyle intervention to improve physical health is central to HF and arrhythmia care and established as a central pillar of management. Mental health represents an important but under-recognised target which requires urgent further investigation.

articles.title: Covert brain infarction in the emergency department: incidence and outcomes.
articles.abstract: Covert brain infarction (CBI) is defined by neuroimaging evidence of cerebral infarction without history of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). The prevalence and management of covert brain infarction in the emergency department (ED) is not well understood. This study aimed to examine the prevalence, management, and one-year outcomes of patients with covert brain infarction detected during ED neuroimaging for non-stroke or TIA reasons. This retrospective observational cohort study included ED patients from two academic hospitals with 24/7 access to computed tomography (CT). The primary outcome was detection of covert brain infarction on CT; secondary outcomes included stroke prevention therapy initiation or modification, specialist referral, and one-year adverse outcomes. Eligible patients were 50 years or older without history of stroke, TIA, or intracranial hemorrhage, who underwent CT in the ED for reasons unrelated to stroke or TIA from January 1 to December 31, 2022. Exclusion criteria included evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or final ED diagnosis of stroke/TIA. Of 6,535 eligible individuals, a total of 102 patients (1.6%) had covert brain infarction detected on neuroimaging. These patients (age: 78.5 ±10.7 years; 61% male) had substantial vascular risk factors, including hypertension (62.7%), dyslipidemia (45.1%), atrial fibrillation (26.5%), diabetes (20.6%), and smoking (41.2%). Prior to ED visit, 18.6% of patients were on antiplatelets and 23.5% were on anticoagulation. Among those with covert brain infarction discharged from the ED, 91.7% received no change in therapy. In one year after the index visit, 1 patient had a stroke/TIA (1.0%), 4 had a myocardial infarction (3.9%), 2 were diagnosed with new atrial fibrillation (2.0%), and 14 died (13.7%). Patients with covert brain infarction detected in the ED had multiple vascular risk factors, and ED physician initiation or modification of new stroke therapy was uncommon, underscoring the need for further characterization and ED-specific pathways for management of this population.

articles.title: Prehospital Advanced Airway Management in Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Cohort Study Using Time-Dependent Propensity Score Sequential Matching.
articles.abstract: Traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (TCA) has extremely poor outcomes, and the benefit of prehospital advanced airway management (AAM) remains uncertain, partly because previous observational studies may have been affected by resuscitation time bias. We examined the association between prehospital AAM and clinical outcomes in adults with TCA using a time-dependent analytic approach. We conducted a nationwide retrospective observational cohort study using the All-Japan Utstein Registry linked with emergency medical services transport records from 2021 to 2023. Adults (≥18 years) with TCA were included. The exposure was successful prehospital AAM, including supraglottic airway placement or endotracheal intubation. The primary outcome was 30-day survival, and the secondary outcome was favorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2) at 30 days. We applied time-dependent propensity score sequential matching and estimated corrected risk differences (RDs) using generalized estimating equations with inverse-frequency weighting. Among 7,217 patients, 2,653 (36.8%) received prehospital AAM, of whom 2,637 were successfully matched within the analytic cohort. Thirty-day survival was 1.8% in the AAM group and 1.4% among matched controls (corrected RD, 0.6%; 95% confidence interval (CI), -0.1 to 1.2). Favorable neurological outcome occurred in 0.2% and 0.4%, respectively (corrected RD, -0.2%; 95% CI, -0.6 to 0.1). No significant timing-dependent association or prespecified subgroup heterogeneity was observed. In this nationwide cohort study using time-dependent propensity score sequential matching, prehospital AAM was not significantly associated with improved outcomes in adults with TCA.

articles.title: Evolution Pattern of High-Altitude Headache: A Prospective Observational Study upon Rapid Ascent to 4300 m.
articles.abstract: IntroductionHeadache is the most common symptom of altitude exposure. However, there have been few studies to observe the evolution and outcomes of high-altitude headache (HAH), and its relationship to acute mountain sickness (AMS), especially following rapid air transport to extreme altitudes.MethodsChinese Han workers who ascended from Lanzhou (1500 m) to the Ali region (4300 m) on the Tibetan Plateau were prospectively studied between March 2023 and May 2025. Clinical features and evolution of altitude headache observed in this cohort at 4300 m were recorded using standardized questionnaires incorporating both the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3) and the 2018 Lake Louise Score (LLS) criteria.ResultsOf the 159 workers, 106 (66.7%) reported headaches on Day 1; the headaches were predominantly bilateral (79.2%) and mild to moderate in intensity (90.5%). Among the 106 participants with headache, 91 (85.8%) fulfilled the LLS criteria for AMS at the same Day 1 assessment. Headache intensity was significantly greater in subjects with AMS compared to those with isolated headache (P = 0.003), but no other headache characteristic differed between groups. The incidence of headache peaked on Day 1 (66.7%) and gradually declined to 0.6% on Day 7, with a median headache duration of 3 days.ConclusionsHAH presents a self-limiting course following acute exposure to high altitude. The clinical overlap with AMS suggests they may reflect different severity of illness rather than separate processes.

articles.title: Reply to: From benchmark success to clinical utility: interpreting large language model performance in emergency department triage.
Clinical behaviors of efficient emergency physicians: insights into what they actually do -a scoping review.
articles.abstract: Efficiency in the emergency department is critical for patient care and flow, yet it is a challenging competency to develop and is inconsistently taught in emergency medicine residency programs. This review focused on identifying strategies and behaviors of efficient emergency physicians that can be observed and taught. A scoping review was conducted from January 1, 2015, to July 1, 2025 following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology, to identify key behaviors of efficient emergency physicians. Medline/PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and gray literature were searched using controlled vocabulary, and included all types of methodologies except editorials and commentaries. Data were extracted using a standardized, structured process within the Covidence platform by two independent reviewers. After screening 6343 articles, 20 articles met full inclusion criteria. A clear and universally accepted definition of emergency department efficiency was not identified. Consequently, the included studies used a heterogeneous range of proxy measures to evaluate efficiency-related outcomes. Although no study directly demonstrated a specific set of strategies that improve efficiency, six major themes emerged. Efficient physicians showed greater effectiveness in communication, targeted investigations, documentation strategies, and clinical teaching skills. In addition, they employed specific cognitive and physical strategies like flow management and movement efficacy. Each theme yielded behaviors that either promoted or impeded efficiency. Although our review identified a limited number of articles linking specific physician behaviors to efficiency metrics, it provides insights into behaviors and strategies that can be taught and observed in emergency physicians. Collectively, the identified strategies suggest that efficiency may largely depend on optimizing the initial patient encounter through communication, clinical reasoning, and shared decision-making. These findings represent the first step in a broader initiative aimed at developing a standardized observational tool to support the development of efficiency in emergency physicians.

articles.title: Sex-based analysis of characteristics, management, and outcomes of patients presenting to the emergency department with syncope.
articles.abstract: Syncope is a common emergency department (ED) presentation and can be caused by serious conditions not evident on initial ED evaluation. Research into sex-based differences among ED patients presenting with syncope is lacking. We sought to compare clinical characteristics, management, risk stratification and serious outcomes between male and female ED syncope patients, assess the impact of sex on outcomes after adjusting for comorbidities and Canadian Syncope Risk Score predictors, and evaluate the change in performance of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score with the addition of sex. We conducted a secondary analysis of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score derivation and validation study cohorts, comparing patient characteristics, ED management and outcomes between male and female patients presenting with syncope, using descriptive statistics and logistic regression models. Of 9539 total patients, 5190 (54.4%) were female. Male patients were older, had more comorbidities, received more testing in the ED, had longer lengths of stay, were more frequently hospitalized and were more likely to have serious outcomes than females. The association between male sex and serious outcomes persisted after controlling for age, arrival by ambulance, hypertension, diabetes, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation or flutter, valvular heart disease, and congestive heart failure (OR=1.73, p<0.001) and Canadian Syncope Risk Score predictors (OR =1.45, p=0.005). However, adding sex to the Canadian Syncope Risk Score model did not significantly increase the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (difference = 0.0002, p=0.90). Male ED syncope patients tended to have more risk factors than females, underwent more investigations, and were more likely to have serious outcomes even when controlling for comorbidities. While clinicians should recognize these sex-based differences, they can continue to rely on the Canadian Syncope Risk Score in its current form for risk stratification as incorporating sex did not improve model performance.

articles.title: Traumatic renal injuries: the prevalence, management and outcome of renal vascular injury.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: To assess the prevalence, management and outcome of renal vascular injuries (RVIs; active bleeding and contained vascular injuries) seen on admission CT. Also, we wanted to find out the prevalence and survival of patients with concomitant injury to liver, spleen, and kidney seen on admission CT. We conducted a retrospective, single-center, longitudinal cohort study with nine-year data (2013-2021) of all ≥ 15-year-old patients with renal injury identified in a trauma registry. Admission CT and angiographic examinations were reviewed to assess RVIs, including active bleeding, arterial dissection, segmental infarct, pseudoaneurysm or AV-fistulae. Medical records were reviewed for treatment, hospital length of stay and 30-day survival rate. Out of 2805 patients with abdominal trauma, 243 (8.7%) had a renal injury, of whom 182 (74.9%) underwent CT on admission. RVI was found in 56 patients (30.8%). Among these 56 patients, 42 (75%) had active bleeding, eight (14.3%) segmental infarct, six (10.7%) pseudoaneurysm, and three (5.4%) arterial dissection. Of these, ten patients (17.9%) underwent angioembolization, and three (5.4%) underwent laparotomy. Patients with RVI were slightly older than those without RVI (43.6 vs. 37.8 years, p = 0.0409) and had more often a penetrating trauma (OR 2.836; 95% CI 1.127-7.136, p = 0.0416). Hospital length of stay (14.7 vs. 14.9 days, p = 0.9520) and 30-day survival (95.2% vs. 92.6%, p = 0.3165) did not differ significantly between patients without and with RVI. Among patients with available CT, fourteen (14/182; 7.7%) had concomitant injuries to the liver, spleen and kidney, with no statistically significant difference in 30-day survival compared with patients without such concomitant injuries (92.9% vs. 94.6%; p = 0.5237). RVI was not uncommon in our study cohort, occurring in 30.8% of patients with renal injury who underwent CT on admission. Of these, 17.9% were treated with angioembolization. Patients with RVI were slightly older and were more likely to have a penetrating injury than patients without RVI. No statistically significant difference in hospital length of stay or 30-day survival was found between patients without and with RVI.

articles.title: Caregiver Perception of Procedural Pain and Health Care Provider Empathy During Pediatric Laceration Repair in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Pediatric laceration repair is a common and distressing emergency department (ED) procedure. Health care provider (HCP) empathy is considered central to family-centered care and perception of HCP empathy is linked to care outcomes, yet perception of HCP empathy surrounding pediatric ED procedures is understudied. We aimed to characterize caregiver perception of HCP empathy following pediatric laceration repair and examine associations with demographics, treatment factors, and procedural pain. This cross-sectional study included a convenience sample of child-caregiver dyads (children 2 to 12 y) undergoing ED laceration repair. Children requiring inpatient admission, with developmental disability, or pain-related chronic illness were excluded. After the procedure, caregivers completed the Jefferson Scale of Patient Perceptions of Physician Empathy (range: 5 to 35). Child procedural pain was assessed via caregiver proxy report (Numeric Rating Scale) and researcher observation (Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability). HCPs self-reported demographics. We performed correlational and mean difference tests to examine associations between variables and caregiver-perceived HCP empathy. The sample included 176 child-caregiver dyads (60% enrollment rate). Mean caregiver-perceived HCP empathy was 28.25±6.10 (range: 5 to 35). Only one empathy item ("understanding doctor") was strongly endorsed by most caregivers (58.8%). Caregiver-reported child procedural pain, but not researcher-observed pain, was negatively associated with perceived HCP empathy (r=-0.18, P=0.03). At the item-level, caregiver-reported child pain was significantly lower when caregivers strongly agreed with 4 of the 5 empathy items (Z's 2.26 to 3.05, P<0.05). Researcher-assessed pain, demographic, or treatment factors (midazolam, length of stay, laceration length) were not associated with perceived HCP empathy (all P>0.05). Modest endorsement across empathy items highlight opportunities to enhance empathic, family-centered care surrounding pediatric ED procedures. Caregiver appraisal of child's pain was the only variable associated with perceived HCP empathy. Strategies targeting empathic pain-related communication may improve families' experiences and perception of care in the pediatric ED.

Prevalence of Persistent Severe Hypertension and Rates of Treatment Among Pregnant Patients in the Prehospital Setting.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) contribute to maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality and require time-sensitive intervention. In April 2025, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), in collaboration with the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP) and the National Association of EMTs (NAEMT), published new guidelines on the prehospital management of elevated blood pressure in pregnancy. The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of persistent severe hypertension among pregnant patients encountered by prehospital clinicians, characterize baseline frequency of pre-guideline treatment, and establish a benchmark to inform implementation of these guidelines. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using the 2024 ESO Data Collaborative public release research dataset (January 1 to December 31, 2024). We identified all 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients documented as pregnant beyond 20 wk of gestation. We excluded injury-related encounters and patients outside the World Health Organization-defined childbearing age range (15 to 49 years). Consistent with the new guidelines, we defined persistent severe hypertension as at least two documented blood pressure measurements with systolic blood pressure ≥ 160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 110 mmHg. We defined guideline-adherent treatment as administration of both magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) and an antihypertensive medication (labetalol, hydralazine, or nifedipine). We identified 39,546 eligible 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients beyond 20 wk of gestation. The prevalence of persistent severe hypertension was 3.1% (n = 1,234/39,546). Among these patients, 77 (6.2%) received magnesium sulfate only, 19 (1.5%) received an antihypertensive medication only, and 10 (0.8%) received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication. Approximately 1 in 32 pregnant patients beyond 20 wk of gestation encountered by prehospital clinicians had persistent severe hypertension. In the year prior to dissemination of the 2025 ACOG, NAEMSP, and NAEMT-supported guidelines, fewer than 1% received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication. These findings establish a national benchmark and identify opportunities to improve prehospital care through protocol development, medication availability, clinician education, and implementation of updated guidelines.

Global, regional, and national burden of non-communicable diseases among adolescents and young adults from 1990 to 2021, with global projections to 2035.
articles.abstract: This study estimated the global, regional, and national burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among adolescents and young adults aged 10-24 years during 1990-2021. Temporal trends were assessed using average annual percentage changes, and Spearman's rank correlation evaluated associations between age-standardized rates and the Socio-demographic Index (SDI). Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models were applied to project global age-standardized rates of mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and years lived with disability (YLDs) through 2035. In 2021, NCDs accounted for approximately 404.87 thousand deaths, 129.49 million DALYs, and 100.62 million YLDs in this population. Neoplasms and cardiovascular diseases were the leading causes of NCD-related death, whereas mental disorders were the predominant source of non-fatal burden. Mortality declined in both absolute numbers and age-standardized rates during 1990-2021, whereas absolute DALYs and YLDs increased despite modest reductions or stability in age-standardized rates. Age-standardized DALY and YLD rates were higher in females, but mortality rates were higher in males. In 2021, age-standardized mortality rates were strongly negatively correlated with SDI at the country level (ρ =- 0.80, P < 0.001), whereas YLD rates showed a moderate positive correlation (ρ = 0.56, P < 0.001). ARIMA projections indicated continued declines in mortality through 2035, with DALY rates remaining stable and YLD rates declining modestly toward pre-pandemic levels. Conclusion: Despite mortality reductions, non-fatal NCD burden driven by mental disorders continues to rise. Marked disparities persist by sex and SDI levels, with high-SDI regions facing escalating disability burden and low-SDI regions confronting elevated mortality. Targeted interventions are urgently needed to advance Sustainable Development Goal Target 3.4.

articles.title: Prehospital Whole Blood Resuscitation in Pediatric Patients: A San Antonio Cohort Descriptive.
articles.abstract: The objective of this study is to describe the demographic, clinical, and prehospital care characteristics of pediatric patients receiving whole blood (WB) resuscitation by San Antonio Fire Department (SAFD). We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study to evaluate pediatric patients who received prehospital low-titer group O positive WB transfusion through the SAFD prehospital blood program between October 2018 and June 2025. The objective was to characterize patient demographics, injury patterns, resuscitative interventions, shock physiology, and outcomes among pediatric recipients in a mature civilian emergency medical services WB program. Of 1703 WB transfusions, 73 (4.3%) were pediatric. Most patients were male (76%), age range 1-17 years old with a mode of 17 years, adolescents represented 78%. Trauma accounted for 96% of cases, firearm injury (74%); all penetrating (84%), blunt (12%), with the remainder classified as medical/unknown. Vascular access was intravenous (73%), intraosseous (26%). Tranexamic acid was co-administered in 39%; 12% received ceftriaxone. When analyzed using age-adjusted Shock Index Pediatric Age-Adjusted (SIPA) thresholds (>1.2 for 1-6 years, >1.0 for 7-12 years, and >0.9 for 13-17 years), based on the initial available prehospital heart rate and systolic blood pressure, 45% of patients had an elevated SIPA, 22% had a normal SIPA, 20% were pulseless and therefore could not undergo SIPA calculation, and 14% lacked sufficient vital-sign data for classification. Survival was 50%; died 39%, and unknown outcomes 11%. Mean delta shock index values were most negative in toddlers (1-4 years) -0.97 ± 1.29, followed by children (5-11 years) -0.76 ± 1.07 and adolescents (12-17 years) -0.16 ± 0.46, indicating a greater physiologic response to resuscitation among younger pediatric patients. Pediatric WB recipients were predominantly adolescent males who sustained penetrating trauma and presented with moderate-to-severe shock. Younger age groups had larger descriptive decreases in shock index during the prehospital encounter; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small subgroup sizes and observational design.

articles.title: Hospital cost structures and resource utilisation across representative treatment pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care: a nationwide DRG-based analysis in Germany.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Implant-associated orthopaedic infections require prolonged inpatient treatment, repeated surgery and multidisciplinary care, yet nationwide evidence on how hospital resources are distributed across clinically distinct treatment pathways is limited. This study characterised hospital-side case costs, resource utilisation and aggregate expenditure across representative German diagnosis-related groups (DRGs) relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care. Publicly available 2024 data from the German Institute for the Hospital Remuneration System (InEK) were analysed. Twelve representative DRGs were selected a priori from official definitions and diagnostic/procedural profiles and grouped into six treatment pathways. The InEK cost matrix reflects standardised hospital-side resource costs from participating calculation hospitals and does not represent actual DRG reimbursement. National case frequencies, length of stay and mean case costs were analysed using frequency-weighted pathway estimates, while pathway-level cost composition was calculated from aggregate component expenditure. The included DRGs represented 36,212 hospitalisations and €305.2 million in aggregate annual hospital-side expenditure represented by the selected DRGs. Mean hospital-side costs ranged from €5,859 to €22,495 per case. Ward care accounted for approximately 34-69% of pathway expenditure; operating theatre services contributed up to 39% in revision arthroplasty. Geriatric rehabilitation generated the largest aggregate expenditure (€119.0 million; 39.0%) because of high case volume, whereas complex vacuum-assisted wound care had the highest per-case cost but only 2.9% of aggregate expenditure. At the aggregated DRG level, mean length of stay was associated with mean case cost (Pearson r = 0.87, 95% CI 0.60-0.96; P < 0.001); leave-one-out correlations ranged from r = 0.79 to r = 0.96. Resource requirements differ markedly across representative DRG pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care. Because the selected DRGs are not infection-exclusive, the reported expenditure should not be interpreted as the national economic burden of implant-associated orthopaedic infection. The findings may inform hospital resource planning and future cost-revenue analyses.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of prehospital capillary high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in patients with acute chest pain: the prospective multicenter VALIDATE study.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) plays a central role in the diagnosis and management of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), including rule-out and rule-in strategies in the emergency department. Extending hs-cTnI testing to the prehospital setting could accelerate patient orientation and clinical decision-making, but the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI remains insufficiently studied. The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. The study is a prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with blinded index test results. Four French emergency medical service systems with 10 mobile intensive care units. Adult patients presenting with acute chest pain were included. Prehospital hs-cTnI measurement using a point-of-care device (Atellica VTLi) on capillary samples. Treating clinicians were blinded to hs-cTnI results. The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. Diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Clinically relevant thresholds were defined a priori based on predefined safety criteria. Among 659 patients included in the primary analysis, 71 (10.8%) had NSTEMI. Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI demonstrated good diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.78-0.88]. A rule-out threshold of <2.2 ng/L, evaluated according to prespecified performance criteria, identified 7.1% of patients, with a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI = 0.92-1.00). A rule-in threshold of >43.6 ng/L identified 6.5% of patients, with a positive predictive value of 0.65 (95% CI = 0.51-0.79). In the predefined sensitivity analysis, venous hs-cTnI showed similar diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI = 0.79-0.89). Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI showed good diagnostic performance for NSTEMI, although feasibility in routine practice was challenged by unavailable or uninterpretable measurements. Further external validation is warranted before implementation in prehospital diagnostic pathways.

articles.title: The "New" Frozen Frontier of World War II: Air War at Extreme Altitude.
articles.abstract: Cold injury was a largely overlooked medical and operational crisis in Allied aviation medicine in the early days of World War II. Although extreme cold had shaped military outcomes for centuries, the rapid ascent of fighting aircraft of this era to altitudes above 8000 m exposed aircrews to unprecedented hypobaric and thermal stress. Early in the conflict, aviation medicine lagged behind engineering advances, and frostbite reached epidemic proportions. The historical record reveals that inadequate equipment, poor training, flawed oxygen-delivery systems, and structural vulnerabilities of aircraft were primary contributors to injury. Moreover, awareness of the mechanisms of cold injury in the early 1940s, at least in the English-speaking world, was at such a basic level that the therapeutic paradigm of rapid rewarming of frostbite injury was not to be readily accepted until the following decade. Nonetheless, the findings of military medical investigators combined with political pressure from civilian consultants prompted high-level review of cold injury in aviators. This ultimately forced reforms at Wright Field, the center of US aeromedical development during the war. Solutions were implemented that included improved oxygen-mask design, protective plexiglass gun-port coverings, individualized cold-weather gear, and mandatory oxygen-use protocols. By mid-1944, frostbite incidence had markedly declined among aircrews. However, the failure to transfer these lessons to ground forces during the winter of 1944 to 1945 underscored persistent gaps in institutional learning and highlighted the need for systematic dissemination of operational medical knowledge across military branches.

Risk Prediction for Heart Failure in Patients with Cancer: Current Models and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Cancer survivors have an elevated risk for developing heart failure due to prior chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and other overlapping co-morbid conditions. With the advancement in cancer treatment, there is an increasing number of survivors who are at an even higher risk of developing heart failure. There is a growing need for heart failure specific risk prediction models in this population to facilitate early diagnosis and timely management. This review aims to summarize most recent findings on heart failure risk prediction among patients with history of cancer. Current risk prediction models focus on heart failure risk at the time of cancer treatment and shortly thereafter. There is limited data on heart failure risk among long term survivors.

articles.title: Airway management during missions of a neurologist-staffed mobile stroke unit: a retrospective registry study.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Following their endorsement by international guidelines, mobile stroke units (MSUs) are increasingly being integrated into emergency medical services worldwide. In real-world use, physician-staffed MSUs can be dispatched beyond their intended indication, exposing on-board neurologists to non-stroke emergencies. This raises important clinical and regulatory questions about the competencies MSU physicians need. Advanced airway management is one of the most critical prehospital interventions. Yet, its frequency, indications, procedural characteristics and success rates have not been investigated in neurologist-staffed MSU services. We retrospectively analysed a prospective registry of mission documentation from a neurologist-staffed MSU service in Berlin, Germany from 31 August 2024 to 15 March 2026. Dispatches of the MSU were classified as stroke or non-stroke dispatches using the recorded activation code. The primary outcome was the dispatch-based frequency of endotracheal intubation (ETI), defined as a documented intubation attempt. All ETIs were performed by the on-board neurologist. Secondary outcomes included supraglottic airway (SGA) use, first-pass success rate, procedural characteristics and self-reported post-mission National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) workload. Proportions are reported with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CI). We analysed 3,887 dispatches. ETI occurred in a total of 49 dispatches (1.26%; 95% CI 0.95-1.66) with 2 in 1,755 stroke- (0.11%; 95% CI 0.03-0.41) and 47 in 2,132 non-stroke dispatches (2.20%; 95% CI 1.66-2.92). SGA use occurred in 22 dispatches (0.57%; 95% CI 0.37-0.86). All 49 intubation attempts were successful (100.0%; 95% CI 92.7-100.0). First-pass success was achieved in 43/49 (87.8%; 95% CI 75.8-94.3) with no ETI requiring more than two attempts. Videolaryngoscopy was used in all ETIs and capnographic confirmation of tube position in 48/49 (98%). Non-traumatic cardiac arrest was the most frequent indication (30/49). In the exploratory workload analysis, the median NASA-TLX score was 59.8 [IQR 50.0-68.7] in 49 dispatches with ETI and 27.0 [15.5-41.7] in 2,700 dispatches without ETI. ETI was infrequent overall and particularly rare during stroke dispatches, yet first-pass success was high. Prospective studies are needed to define airway management requirements and training standards for MSU physicians.

articles.title: Adaptive Workforce Strategies in Public Health Emergencies: A Quasi-Experimental Study with a Historical Control Group.
articles.abstract: Crisis-driven health care shortages require adaptive regulatory changes. Allowing advanced nursing students to provide clinical care could bolster surge capacity while enhancing professional competence. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of crisis period clinical work on nursing students' academic and licensure outcomes. A quasi-experimental study with a historical control group was conducted among 68 students enrolled in an academic career retraining track (an intensive first-entry nursing program for individuals holding a non-nursing bachelor's degree with no prior nursing background). During a major public health emergency (the COVID-19 pandemic), a work experience group (n = 23) received temporary clinical permissions before licensure, while a control group (n = 45) followed the standard curriculum without early clinical employment. Outcomes included final program grades and scores on the Governmental Licensing Examination in Nursing (GLEIN). The work experience group demonstrated significantly higher mean final grades [79.92 (SD = 5.14) versus 76.9 (SD = 9.72); difference, 3.02 (95% CI, 0.28-5.76); P =.033] and higher GLEIN scores [81.85 (SD = 6.69) versus 73.9 (SD = 9.49); difference, 7.95 (95% CI, 0.70-15.20); P =.029] compared to the control group. Regression analysis identified crisis period clinical work experience as a significant predictor of higher licensing exam performance. Temporary clinical employment of advanced nursing students during a crisis was positively associated with academic performance and higher licensing examination scores. Adaptive regulatory policies can support student academic readiness and licensure success during public health emergencies.

Preoperative CT-derived psoas attenuation and correction loss after traumatic thoracolumbar fracture fixation: A construct-dependent association.
articles.abstract: Postoperative correction loss remains a concern after posterior fixation of traumatic thoracolumbar fractures. Although bone quality and construct characteristics influence mechanical stability, the role of preoperative muscle quality remains poorly defined. We examined whether CT-derived psoas attenuation was associated with correction loss and whether fracture-level screw placement modified this association. This retrospective single-center cohort included 78 adults who underwent posterior pedicle screw fixation for traumatic AO Spine A3 thoracolumbar fractures. Preoperative psoas and paravertebral attenuation and cross-sectional area were measured at L3. Correction loss was defined as the difference between final-follow-up and immediate postoperative Cobb angles measured on supine sagittal CT reconstructions. Multivariable linear regression tested the interaction between centered psoas attenuation and fracture-level screw placement, adjusting for age, sex, vertebral attenuation, instrumented levels, and follow-up duration. An extended model added vertebral height loss and canal compromise. HC3 robust variance estimation and sensitivity analyses were performed. Mean correction loss was 4.1 ± 5.4°, and 23 patients (29.5%) experienced loss greater than 5°. The psoas attenuation-by-fracture-level screw interaction was significant (B=0.311°/HU; 95% CI, 0.091-0.530; p = .006; HC3 p = .037). Without fracture-level screws, each 10-HU increase in psoas attenuation corresponded to approximately 2.6° less correction loss (B=-0.255°/HU; 95% CI, -0.440 to -0.071; p = .007), although HC3 inference crossed the null (p = .068). No clear association was observed with fracture-level screws. The interaction persisted after adjustment for vertebral height loss and canal compromise (B=0.342°/HU; 95% CI, 0.127-0.556; p = .002; HC3 p = .016), when short- versus long-segment fixation replaced instrumented-level count, and in patients with at least 12 months of follow-up. Paravertebral attenuation showed a similar pattern, whereas muscle cross-sectional area did not. Preoperative psoas attenuation showed a construct-dependent association with correction loss after fixation of traumatic AO Spine A3 fractures. Lower attenuation may identify mechanical vulnerability when the fractured vertebra is not incorporated into the construct. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before CT-based muscle assessment can guide construct selection.

articles.title: To cradle or not: assessing the use of a lumbar puncture cradle on lumbar puncture success rates.
articles.abstract: Neonatal and infant lumbar puncture success rates range from 50 to 80%, while traumatic lumbar punctures are reported in 30-50%. A novel lumbar puncture cradle, SMöLTAP®, designed to standardize seated positioning may improve procedural outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the first-pass success and traumatic lumbar puncture rates using the cradle compared to the lateral decubitus. This was a single-center cohort study from August 2020-October 2024 in a tertiary pediatric emergency department. Term and corrected preterm infants (≥ 37 weeks, ≤ 3 months) requiring a lumbar puncture were identified through an EPIC report. Unstable infants, those requiring opening pressure, performed under sedation or using ultrasound guidance, and charts with missing documentation were excluded. Lumbar punctures using the cradle were identified first, and a stratified random sampling technique was used to select the non-exposed cohort, in which lumbar punctures were performed in the lateral decubitus position. Chi-square analysis and logistic regression were used to analyze lumbar puncture success rates. 142 infants were included (mean age 26 days, 57% male). Cradle use was associated with a higher first-pass success rate: 63%, as opposed to 41% in the control lateral decubitus group p = 0.01. It remained significantly associated with first-pass success after a multivariable logistic regression (OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.06-4.68, p = 0.03). Cradle use was associated with fewer traumatic lumbar punctures, 36% versus 59% (p = 0.01), percent difference 23% (95% CI 6.6-37.8). There was no difference in the overall success rate, 80% versus 70%, p = 0.17. The cradle is a promising tool that may improve first-pass success, reduce traumatic lumbar punctures, and provide more precise management of febrile infants requiring a lumbar puncture, thereby reducing clinical diagnostic and management challenges.

articles.title: A Retrospective Study of the Efficacy of Regional Anesthesia in Reducing Donor Site Harvest Pain in Burn Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Despite advances in burn care, the pain of burn treatment remains unresolved. The creation of donor harvest sites is often unavoidable, and the subsequent pain is difficult to treat. Regional anesthesia for the donor harvest sites can provide effective analgesia, however, there is limited literature regarding its efficacy. The purpose of this study was to assess the use of regional anesthesia for donor harvest site pain. Patients admitted to the burn center from January 1, 2011, to May 15, 2025, with thigh donor site harvest(s) were reviewed for study inclusion. Data collected included demographics, burn variables, hospital course data, and regional anesthesia procedure details. Descriptive statistics were used to determine differences between the block and non-block groups. Of the 524 patients included, 164 (31.3%) had donor site blocks and 360 (68.7%) did not. There were 77 (47%) with single shot blocks and 87 (53%) had indwelling catheters (groin or epidural). The groups were well-matched in their demographics, burn injury data, and hospital variables. The overall oral morphine equivalents (OME) and pain report levels were similar between the block and control groups in all three post-operative periods. However, causal conclusions are limited by this retrospective, heterogenous study. An appropriately protocolized prospective study is planned.

articles.title: Predictors and clinical outcomes of extubation failure in patients with cervical spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract: Respiratory compromise is common in cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) and poses a challenge in deciding whether to extubate or perform a tracheostomy. This study evaluated the characteristics of failed extubations and hypothesized that those with unsuccessful extubation attempts would have a higher trauma burden and worse weaning parameters. This was a retrospective review of intubated cervical SCI at a Level 1 trauma center from 2018 to 2024. Demographics, injury, surgical and airway management data were collected. Location of intubation and extubation, weaning parameters, and time to airway event or failure were tabulated. Statistical analysis was completed using Stata with p < 0.05 as significant. Seventy patients with SCI were analyzed with a mean age of 54 years (range 18-89) and 62 (89%) males. Twenty successful extubations (SE) were compared to 36 failed extubations (FE), excluding the direct to tracheostomy (10) or terminally extubated (4) patients. Frequency of TBI (5% FE vs 14% SE, p = 0.3), blunt cerebrovascular injury (25% vs. 32%, p = 0.63) and ISS (30 vs 23, p = 0.13) were not statistically different. Documented weaning parameters - rapid shallow breathing index and negative inspiratory force were similar, although more FE patients were extubated in the OR/PACU. FE patients had significantly fewer hospital and ICU-free days; however, mortality differences did not reach statistical significance. Failed extubation in SCI is associated with longer length of stay. Trauma burden and weaning parameters were not correlated with FE; however, extubation outside of the ICU may increase the risk of failure.

articles.title: Comparative mortality of pelvic ring fractures vs. hip fractures in adults ≥55 years: A propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: Hip and pelvic fragility fractures are associated with substantial mortality in older adults. While standardized care pathways are established for hip fractures, management of pelvic fragility fractures remains less defined. This study compared mortality between matched hip and pelvic ring fracture patients managed operatively or nonoperatively. Pelvic and hip fractures would demonstrate comparable mortality within operative and nonoperative treatment groups. This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX network to identify adults aged ≥ 55 years with hip or pelvic ring fractures. Patients were stratified by operative or nonoperative management, and cohorts were propensity score matched 1:1 based on demographic and clinical characteristics. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were mortality at 30 days, 90 days, and 2 years. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated 1-year mortality. After matching, 255,202 patients per cohort were included in the nonoperative subgroup and 11,448 per cohort in the operative subgroup. Among nonoperative patients, 1-year mortality was higher after hip than pelvic fracture (11.13% vs 10.68%; HR 1.123, 95% CI 1.105-1.141). Among operative patients, 1-year mortality was also higher after hip fracture (8.84% vs 5.94%; HR 1.424, 95% CI 1.314-1.545). However, 30-day mortality was higher after operative pelvic fracture (3.11% vs 2.49%; p = 0.004). Male sex, older age, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease were associated with increased mortality. Hip fractures were associated with greater 1-year mortality across management strategies; however, operative pelvic fractures demonstrated greater early mortality. These findings highlight pelvic fragility fractures as high-risk injuries warranting further evaluation of standardized geriatric care pathways. III.

articles.title: Beyond conventional trauma planning: Integrating geographic and seasonal risk patterns into traumatic spinal injury preparedness.
A bedside score using arrival data to identify major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring fracture: Development and validation.
articles.abstract: Early recognition of major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring injury could guide mobilization of transfusion and hemorrhage-control resources. We developed an arrival-based bedside score and compared its performance with shock index. We studied 239,736 adults with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures in the 2019-2024 National Trauma Data Bank. Major hemorrhage was defined as a hemorrhage-control procedure, hemorrhagic death, or transfusion of ≥ 1000 mL or ≥ 4 units of red blood cells within 4 h. Penalized logistic regression selected arrival variables for an integer score. We assessed performance in a held-out test set (n = 79,912) and at approximately matched alert volume. A model refitted on 2019-2022 admissions was evaluated in 2023-2024. Subgroup analyses were post hoc. Major hemorrhage occurred in 26,479 patients (11.0%); 31.0% were aged ≥ 75 years, and 45.9% had fallen. In the test set, the score achieved an AUROC of 0.882 (95% CI, 0.879-0.886), exceeding shock index by 0.060 (95% CI, 0.055-0.064; P < 0.001). At approximately 15.6% of patients flagged, the score identified 678 additional major hemorrhage cases with 684 fewer false-positive alerts. The temporally validated model achieved an AUROC of 0.885 (95% CI, 0.881-0.888). Discrimination exceeded shock index for pelvic ring disruption (0.830 vs 0.778) and high-energy mechanisms (0.811 vs 0.764), but was lower after falls (0.779 vs 0.800). In patients with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures, an arrival-based score identified major hemorrhage more accurately than shock index at a similar alert burden. Reduced performance after falls and uncertain applicability to suspected fractures warrant caution. External validation and prospective impact assessment are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Does the number of debridement procedures impact risk of infection in open fractures?
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between the number of debridements and risk of infection, while stratifying by degree of wound contamination. It was hypothesized that patients with severe contamination, a higher number of debridements would be associated with lower risk of infection. This is a retrospective secondary analysis of prospectively collected data in the PREP-IT trial (Program of Randomized trials to Evaluate Preoperative antiseptic skin solutions in orthopaedic Trauma). The primary outcome measure was adjudicated surgical site infection. Independent variables were number of debridement procedures and time from injury to definitive wound closure. Analysis was stratified by degree of contamination and multivariable analyses were performed to control for confounders. 3502 total open fractures corresponding to 3222 patients with a median (interquartile range, IQR) age of 42 (29-58) years (2199 [62.8%] men; median (IQR) body mass index 27.7 [24.3-32.6]) were included in this analysis. 2199 patients were included in the non/minimal contamination group, 970 in the surface contamination group, and 333 in the embedded contamination group. After controlling for patient-level characteristics there was a 27% increase in the risk of infection for each debridement performed in the overall patient cohort (OR 1.27 [1.12-1.43] p < 0.001), and a 45% increase in the embedded contamination group (OR, 1.45 [1.12-1.88] p = 0.004). There was no statistically significant difference between minimal contamination groups and the surface contamination group. The results of this study indicate that increased number of debridement procedures was not associated with lower infectious rates. Patients with the highest degree of contamination demonstrated significantly increased risk of developing an infection with each additional debridement. These findings support the importance of limiting unnecessary additional debridement procedures to reduce infection risk and optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Cone-Beam CT-Guided SpineJack® vertebral augmentation: A reproducible technique for accurate pedicular access and implant deployment.
articles.abstract: SpineJack® vertebral augmentation requires precise bilateral transpedicular access and accurate implant deployment. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and technical performance of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-guided SpineJack augmentation. This retrospective single-institution, two-site study included consecutive CBCT-guided procedures performed between May 2021 and April 2026. Technical success required planned bilateral implantation, expansion, and cement augmentation without pedicle breach or implant malposition on final CBCT. Secondary outcomes included immediate vertebral height restoration, complications, procedure duration, radiation exposure, and treatment setting. The analysis included 178 procedures; median age was 45 years (interquartile range [IQR], 27-59), and 158 procedures (88.8%) involved traumatic fractures. Technical success was 100% (178/178), including 64 procedures (36.0%) with pedicle-implant clearance < 0.8 mm. Median absolute vertebral body height gain was 4.1 mm (IQR, 2.7-6.1), and median restoration of baseline height loss reached 77% (IQR, 47-98). All 24 cement leaks (13.5%) were asymptomatic. No neurological, vascular, infectious, or implant-related complications occurred. Median procedure duration was 60 min (IQR, 50-90), and median dose-area product was 33.2 Gy·cm² (IQR, 19.4-53.1). One hundred procedures (56.2%) were performed on an outpatient basis. CBCT-guided SpineJack augmentation achieved accurate bilateral implant deployment and substantial immediate vertebral height restoration without major procedure-related complications. These findings support CBCT as a reliable guidance strategy for vertebral augmentation, with demonstrated feasibility in outpatient practice.

articles.title: The MIS-Diamond fixation: A minimally invasive diamond-shaped construct for spinopelvic dissociation in polytrauma patients.
articles.abstract: Sacral fracture with spinopelvic dissociation (SPD) is a rare, high-energy injury associated with substantial mortality and morbidity. Surgical stabilization is technically challenging and has historically been associated with relatively high rates of construct failure. The present study describes and evaluates a novel minimally invasive spinopelvic diamond-shaped construct (The MIS-Diamond fixation), designed to improve rigid triangular stabilization while minimizing soft-tissue morbidity and facilitate the fracture reduction. A retrospective observational study was conducted including patients who underwent MIS-Diamond fixation for AO Type C3 sacral fractures at a single Level-I Trauma Center between January 2014 and December 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Neurological status, operative parameters, perioperative complications, and radiological outcomes were systematically assessed. Fractures were classified according to the AO Spine Sacral Injury Classification System. Thirty-two patients (mean age 39 years) were included. Surgery was performed at a median of 5 days post-injury, with a mean operative time of 115.8 min and mean estimated blood loss of 82.7 mL. No intraoperative complications occurred. One patient developed a postoperative S1 motor impairment attributed to indirect radicular injury during reduction. Implant-related complications were recorded in 4 patients (12.5%), including one late-onset surgical site infection and three cases of asymptomatic iliac screw loosening. No soft tissue or wound healing complications were observed. Implant removal was successfully completed in 28 patients (87.5%) at 12 months postoperatively. MIS-Diamond fixation demonstrated a favourable safety profile while enabling early postoperative mobilization. The incorporation of a 5.5 mm transverse iliac rod converts the classical triangular construct into a rigid box-like configuration, enhancing rotational stability and preventing coronal diastasis during vertical distraction. Limiting instrumentation to L4-L5 reduces the number of immobilized motion segments compared to previously described longer constructs, potentially mitigating long-term degenerative sequelae. The MIS-Diamond fixation represents a safe and effective minimally invasive surgical option for SPD, providing reliable multiplanar stabilization with a low complication profile. Routine implant removal at 12 months is feasible and recommended to preserve motion segment function. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to further validate these findings.

articles.title: Transanal irrigation to treat refractory constipation: a short-term real-life study.
articles.abstract: The treatment of patients complaining of chronic constipation is still far from ideal, and there is a discrete percentage of them that are labeled as refractory to the usual therapeutic approaches. In these patients there is often the need to use alternative approaches. Among these, transanal irrigation seems promising. Our aim was to evaluate the effect of transanal irrigation on symptoms and quality of life in patients with severe refractory constipation. To this end, we retrospectively analyzed the charts of 31 such patients undergoing transanal irrigation, and evaluated them basally and one and three months after the treatment. Data were collected by means of the Wexner score and the SF12 questionnaire for quality of life. Overall, there was a significant decrease of the constipation scores and an improvement of quality of life score after treatment, after both one and three months. No important side effects were documented. In conclusion, treatment with transanal irrigation may be useful, alone or as combination therapy, in patients with constipation refractory to the conventional therapeutic approaches, but studies in more numerous cohorts of subjects are needed to firmly validate this approach.

Pharmacological Management of Atrial Fibrillation Across the Heart Failure Ejection Fraction Spectrum: Rate Control, Rhythm Control, and Beyond.
articles.abstract: To summarise the contemporary pharmacological management of atrial fibrillation (AF) in heart failure (HF), focusing on rate and rhythm control and upstream therapies across the ejection fraction spectrum. Rate control remains a cornerstone of AF management, particularly in permanent AF or haemodynamically fragile patients, with beta-blockers, digoxin, and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers selected according to ejection fraction phenotype. Concurrently, increasing evidence supports early rhythm-control strategies because of their prognostic benefits in HF populations, with current guidelines reinforcing a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-guided approach to antiarrhythmic drug selection. Beyond conventional drugs, HF guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is emerging as an important upstream pharmacological strategy for modulation of the arrhythmogenic substrate. AF management in HF requires an integrated, phenotype-oriented approach combining symptom control, thromboembolic prevention, and optimisation of GDMT. LVEF remains a key determinant of pharmacological safety and therapeutic selection, whereas haemodynamic status primarily guides acute management decisions.

articles.title: Female Fingerprint: Sex-Specific Aspects in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist and represent a major source of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review summarizes current evidence on sex-specific differences in epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, and treatment in women with AF and HF. Emerging evidence indicates that women with AF and HF constitute a distinct clinical and biological phenotype. Women typically develop AF at older age, more commonly present with hypertension and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and report greater symptom burden and impaired quality of life. Sex-specific mechanisms including hormonal influences, atrial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, and microvascular disease contribute to these differences. Population studies further demonstrate sex-related disparities in HF development and outcomes across AF subtypes. Despite increasing awareness, women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and are less likely to receive rhythm-control strategies, catheter ablation, or device therapy. Recognition of the "female fingerprint" in AF and HF is essential for individualized risk stratification and the advancement of precision cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: Understanding the Partner Landscape for Zoonotic Diseases and Public Health Emergency Preparedness Capacity Strengthening Efforts in Ethiopia.
articles.abstract: Multisectoral collaboration is critical for improving global health security; however, little has been known about how it occurs in order to strengthen public health capacities in low-income settings. We used a multiple case study design to explore multisectoral collaboration in Ethiopia for strengthening public health capacities in 2 cases: public health emergency preparedness and zoonotic diseases. Document analysis and in-depth interviews identified partners for each case and examined partner roles and responsibilities. Partners perceived Ethiopian government entities as leading capacity development, and multisectoral collaboration as important to efforts. Platforms convening sectors and partners, such as the National One Health Steering Committee, were important collaboration facilitators. Institutionalizing multisectoral collaboration can improve leadership awareness and commitment to collaboration. A common understanding of roles and responsibilities in collaboration efforts can also improve accountability, sustainability, and trust. Research findings can improve understanding of how multisectoral collaboration occurs in Ethiopia for public health capacity development. Findings can also provide considerations for strengthening and leveraging multisectoral collaboration to improve public health capacities and systems in other low-income settings. Additional research can expand the evidence base for how multisectoral collaboration increases global health security.
